# Antares

<Meta title="Welcome" />

# Antares

A collection of accessible, composable React components built on React Aria.

[Documentation](https://godaddy.github.io/antares) | [Storybook](https://godaddy.github.io/antares/storybook)

## Quick Start [#quick-start]

Install the package:

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

Import and use a component:

```tsx
import { Button } from '@godaddy/antares';

export default function App() {
  return <Button variant="primary">Get Started</Button>;
}
```

### Per-Component Imports [#per-component-imports]

Each component is available as a standalone entry point. This lets your bundler load only the JavaScript and CSS for the components you use:

```tsx
import { Button } from '@godaddy/antares/Button';
import { Flex } from '@godaddy/antares/Layout';
import { BarChart } from '@godaddy/antares/Chart';
```

This also works with autocomplete in IDEs and LLMs, so you can import from the root package and let your editor/agent suggest the available components.

## Framework Setup [#framework-setup]

Antares ships CSS alongside its JavaScript modules. Each component chunk imports a corresponding `.css` file (e.g., `import './src-BZhWcxqJ.css'`). Most bundlers handle this automatically, but some frameworks need extra configuration to process CSS imports from `node_modules`.

### Next.js [#nextjs]

Add `@godaddy/antares` to [`transpilePackages`](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/transpilePackages) so Next.js processes the package through its own CSS pipeline instead of treating it as a pre-built external:

```js
// next.config.js
/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
const nextConfig = {
  transpilePackages: ['@godaddy/antares'],
};

module.exports = nextConfig;
```

Without this, Next.js will throw:

```text
Global CSS cannot be imported from within node_modules.
```

### Remix [#remix]

Remix with Vite handles CSS imports from `node_modules` in the client bundle automatically. However, during SSR, Vite treats `node_modules` as externals by default, which bypasses CSS processing. Add `@godaddy/antares` to [`ssr.noExternal`](https://vite.dev/config/ssr-options#ssr-noexternal) to fix this:

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';

export default defineConfig({
  ssr: {
    noExternal: ['@godaddy/antares'],
  },
});
```

### Vite [#vite]

Vite processes CSS imports from `node_modules` out of the box. No additional configuration is needed for client-side SPAs.

If you are using Vite with SSR (e.g., custom SSR setup, not Remix), add `@godaddy/antares` to `ssr.noExternal` as shown in the [Remix section](#remix).

### Other Bundlers [#other-bundlers]

Any bundler that supports CSS imports will work with Antares. If your bundler does not process CSS imports from `node_modules` by default, ensure it is configured to do so. For example, with raw webpack you may need [`css-loader`](https://webpack.js.org/loaders/css-loader/) configured to handle `.css` files from `node_modules`.

# Accordion

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- Single or multiple expanded sections.
- Controlled and uncontrolled group state.
- Group-level disabled state.
- Composable sections using Collapsible and CollapsiblePanel.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Customization [#customization]

Compose related `Collapsible` sections inside Accordion. Give each section a stable, unique `id`.
See the Collapsible component documentation for more information about section anatomy, panel content, and trigger styling.

Use `defaultExpandedKeys` for initial expansion, or `expandedKeys` with `onExpandedChange` for
controlled state. Keys must match the section IDs; the callback receives a `Set` of expanded keys.
By default, only one section can stay open. Set `allowsMultipleExpanded` to keep several open.
Both behaviors are shown in the examples.

Use `className` and `style` to customize the group container. `data-disabled` reflects the group's
disabled state. Customize individual headings, triggers, and panels on the composed Collapsible sections.

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard [#keyboard]

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` / `Shift + Tab` | Move between enabled triggers and controls in expanded panels |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Toggle the focused section; focus stays on the trigger |

### ARIA [#aria]

- Each section's trigger is a native button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` linked to its panel.
- Each panel is labeled by its trigger through `aria-labelledby` automatically.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Group related sections and keep essential information visible outside the accordion.
- Use descriptive section titles and heading levels that fit the page hierarchy.
- Use multiple expansion when users need to compare information across sections.
- Keep item IDs stable when reordering or filtering data.
- Manage expansion on Accordion when sections belong to a group.
- Keep form validation and step progression in application logic.

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### Controlled State Not Updating [#controlled-state-not-updating]

Update `expandedKeys` from `onExpandedChange` and make sure the keys match the item IDs.
Changing `defaultExpandedKeys` after mounting does not control expansion.

### Sections Close When Another Opens [#sections-close-when-another-opens]

Enable `allowsMultipleExpanded` when several sections should remain open together.
For a single independent section, use Collapsible without an Accordion.

## Props [#props]

```tsx
<Accordion>
  <Collapsible>
    <Heading>
      <Button slot="trigger">
        <Text />
        <Icon slot="indicator" />
      </Button>
    </Heading>
    <CollapsiblePanel>{/* ... */}</CollapsiblePanel>
  </Collapsible>
</Accordion>;
```

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />


# Alert

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard [#keyboard]

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus to the dismiss button or action button |
| `Space` / `Enter` | Activates the focused button |

### Screen readers [#screen-readers]

The alert container uses `role="alert"`, which creates an ARIA live region. When an alert is rendered or its content changes, screen readers announce the message automatically — the user does not need to navigate to the alert to hear it.

### Dismiss button label [#dismiss-button-label]

The dismiss button defaults to `aria-label="Close"`. Override it via `ariaLabels={{ close: '...' }}` to provide more specific context for screen readers (e.g. `"Dismiss payment warning"`). This is especially useful when multiple alerts are visible at the same time.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Write alert content from the user's perspective: describe what happened and what they can do next, not the underlying technical error.
- Use `critical` only when the user truly cannot continue without resolving the issue. Overusing it reduces its impact.
- Always provide a `title` when the alert includes a dismiss button — it improves the reading experience for screen reader users.
- When using `actions`, prefer `secondary` or `tertiary` Button variants. Avoid placing a primary action inside an alert.
- Do not stack multiple alerts of the same emphasis; consolidate the message into a single alert.

## Props [#props]

### Alert [#alert]

# Avatar

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- Composable `Avatar`, `Image`, and `Text` parts
- Circle and rounded-square shapes at four named sizes
- Automatic image loading with a Text monogram fallback
- Primary, subtle, and 15 categorical figure emphases
- Avatar Button and Account Menu compositions built with Pressable

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Customization [#customization]

Use Image native image props for responsive image sources. Choose a deterministic `figure0` through `figure14` emphasis in lists that categorize multiple entities.

When an Avatar triggers an action, compose it with `Pressable` so the Avatar keeps its own shape and receives the interaction behavior directly. Use this pattern for an Avatar Button, or place it inside `MenuTrigger` for an Account Menu:

```tsx
<Pressable aria-label="Account menu" onPress={openAccountMenu}>
  <Avatar role="button">
    <Text>UT</Text>
  </Avatar>
</Pressable>
```

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

- Give Image meaningful `alt` text when the image conveys an identity.
- Text remains available to assistive technology when no image loads.
- Use `alt=""` on the Image and `aria-hidden="true"` on the Avatar when the entire avatar is purely decorative.
- Give an Avatar Button or Account Menu an accessible name with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- When using `Pressable`, provide an interactive role for the non-semantic Avatar child.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Use Avatar for informational identity; compose it with `Pressable` for an Avatar Button or Account Menu when it is independently actionable.
- Use circle for people and square for businesses, workspaces, and accounts.
- Keep monograms to one or two uppercase characters.
- Use the same `figure*` emphasis for the same entity wherever it appears.

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

- If an image is unavailable because of a bad URL or CORS policy, Text remains visible.
- Long Text content is clipped to the avatar shape; provide a one- or two-character monogram.
- Figure colors repeat after 15 values; assign a deterministic figure emphasis in the consuming application.

## Props [#props]

```tsx
<Avatar>
  <Image />
  <Text />
</Avatar>
```

### Avatar [#avatar]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />


# Button

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

Use the `LinkButton` component instead when you need navigation functionality with a button-like appearance.

Use `target="_blank"` to open a link in a new tab without an icon. `isExternal` adds an icon and defaults
to `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`; explicit `target` and `rel` override those defaults.
You can also compose an `Icon` as a child independently of navigation behavior.

Use the `CloseButton` preset to dismiss an overlay (such as a `Modal`). It defaults to `slot="close"`, so it picks up the overlay's close behavior with no wiring, and always renders an `x` icon with `aria-label="Close"`. For a labelled dismiss action (e.g. "Cancel"), use a raw `<Button slot="close">Cancel</Button>`.

Inside a field `Group`, `slot="control"` and `slot="trigger"` pick up the matching look, size, and
disabled state from context. See TextField for control affixes, and Select or DatePicker for trigger faces.
The `control` and `trigger` variants are field parts: the field sizes them, so use them only inside a field.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Props [#props]

### Button [#button]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />

### LinkButton [#linkbutton]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.LinkButtonProps} />

### CloseButton [#closebutton]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.CloseButtonProps} />


# Calendar

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- Single-date (`Calendar`) and range (`RangeCalendar`) grids built on React Aria
- Month dropdown plus a typeable year input in the header for fast navigation
- Keyboard navigable and screen-reader announced
- `minValue` / `maxValue` bounds and `isDateUnavailable` per-day disabling
- Date-only values via `@internationalized/date`'s `CalendarDate`

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install @godaddy/antares
```

## Working with dates [#working-with-dates]

`Calendar` values are `CalendarDate` objects. Import the date primitives you need from the `@godaddy/antares/date` subpath:

```tsx
import { parseDate, today, getLocalTimeZone } from '@godaddy/antares/date';
import { Calendar } from '@godaddy/antares';

<Calendar aria-label="Date" defaultValue={parseDate('2024-03-15')} />;
<Calendar aria-label="Today" defaultValue={today(getLocalTimeZone())} />;
```

`@godaddy/antares/date` re-exports [`@internationalized/date`](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/internationalized/date/), the package behind these date primitives.

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

- Arrow keys move by day; PageUp/PageDown by month; Home/End to row edges
- Focus-visible outline; disabled days are not focusable
- Out-of-month days are hidden and are not selectable
- Unavailable days are struck through; days outside the date bounds render at reduced opacity

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Always provide an `aria-label` on standalone calendars.
- Use `isDateUnavailable` for scattered disabled days; use `minValue` / `maxValue` for contiguous bounds.

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

- Dates not formatting per locale? Ensure the app is wrapped in `<I18nProvider locale="…">`.

## Props [#props]

### Calendar [#calendar]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />

### RangeCalendar [#rangecalendar]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.RangeCalendarProps} />


# Card

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

Card groups related content, like media, text, and actions, on a single surface. On its own, a Card
is a static surface, or a link when you pass `href`. Put Cards in a `CardGroup` to make them
selectable or to give them an action: the group owns selection, row actions, focus, and arrow-key
navigation.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Customization [#customization]

Customize `CardSelectionIndicator` with non-interactive children or a selection-state render
function. `CardGroup` owns selection, which works without an indicator.

Use `className` with `[data-selected]`, `[data-hovered]`, `[data-pressed]`, `[data-focus-visible]`,
and `[data-disabled]` to style Card states.

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

- Name `CardGroup` with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, and set `textValue` on Cards with composed
  content for accessible names and typeahead.
- `CardGroup` uses grid navigation: Tab enters or leaves, arrow keys move between Cards, and Space
  changes selection. Enter activates row actions or links. Choose selection or `onAction`;
  combining them prevents pointer selection.
- Use `keyboardNavigationBehavior="tab"` for nested controls. Antares controls keep their actions
  independent of the Card; use `Pressable` for custom controls.
- A standalone Card with `href` is a link and must not contain buttons, inputs, or other controls.

## Props [#props]

```tsx
<CardGroup selectionMode="multiple">
  <Card id="privacy" textValue="Domain privacy">
    <CornerActions />
    <Image />
    <TextLockup />
    {/* ... */}
  </Card>
</CardGroup>
```

### Card [#card]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />

### CardGroup [#cardgroup]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.CardGroupProps} />

### CardSelectionIndicator [#cardselectionindicator]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.CardSelectionIndicatorProps} />

# Bar Chart

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- **Single and multi-series support**: Display one or multiple data series with grouped bars
- **Vertical and horizontal orientations**: Choose the best layout for your data and use case
- **Responsive behavior**: Auto-sizing with horizontal scrolling for many data points, sticky axes
- **Design system alignment**: 8px border radius, 12px bar width (1.5 GU), consistent spacing
- **Interactive tooltips**: Hover to see exact values, with smart positioning and scroll-awareness
- **Customizable axes**: Control gridlines, tick marks, axis titles, and tick formatting
- **Custom domains**: Set explicit x and y ranges for controlled scales across multiple charts
- **RTL support**: Full right-to-left layout support for international audiences _(in development)_
- **Accessibility ready**: Keyboard navigation, screen reader support, and semantic HTML
- **TypeScript support**: Fully typed with comprehensive prop interfaces
- **VisX integration**: Leverages VisX primitives for scales, axes, shapes, and responsive layout

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Design System Alignment [#design-system-alignment]

### Spacing and Sizing [#spacing-and-sizing]

- **Bar width**: 12px (1.5 grid units)
- **Bar padding** (multi-series): 4px between bars within a group
- **Group gap**: Minimum 24px between bar groups
- **Border radius**: 8px on all bars
- **Margins**: 20px top/right, 60px bottom/left for axes and labels

### Responsive Behavior [#responsive-behavior]

- **Auto-sizing**: Uses VisX's `useParentSize` hook to adapt to container width
- **Horizontal scrolling**: When data points exceed available width, the chart becomes horizontally scrollable
- **Sticky y-axis**: The y-axis remains visible during horizontal scroll
- **Minimum spacing**: Group gaps never fall below 24px, triggering scroll instead

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

- **Keyboard navigation**: Bar groups are keyboard accessible with `tabIndex={0}` and `role="group"`
- **Screen reader support**: Semantic HTML structure with proper ARIA attributes
- **Tooltips**: Show on both hover and focus for keyboard users

## Performance Considerations [#performance-considerations]

### Rendering Strategy [#rendering-strategy]

The component uses VisX primitives for optimal SVG rendering:

- **Scales**: VisX's `scaleBand` and `scaleLinear` for efficient coordinate mapping
- **Grouped rendering**: Bars are rendered in SVG `<Group>` elements for logical organization
- **Responsive sizing**: `useParentSize` hook provides efficient resize detection with debouncing (15ms)

### Scrolling Strategy [#scrolling-strategy]

- **Vertical charts**: Horizontal scrolling when many data points exceed container width
- **Horizontal charts**: Vertical scrolling when many categories exceed container height
- **Sticky axes**: Positioned absolutely to remain visible during scroll

### Recommendations [#recommendations]

- For charts with **many data points** (>20), consider enabling horizontal scroll (default behavior)
- For **horizontal bar charts**, vertical scrolling is more mobile-friendly than horizontal
- Use **custom domains** to maintain consistent scales across multiple charts
- **Tooltips** use absolute positioning and scroll-aware calculations for accurate placement

## Development Status [#development-status]

The BarChart component is in active development. Current focus areas:

- ✅ Single and multi-series support
- ✅ Vertical and horizontal orientations
- ✅ Responsive behavior with sticky axes
- ✅ Interactive tooltips
- ✅ Custom domains
- ✅ Design system alignment
- 🚧 RTL compatibility (axis rendering and spacing refinement)
- 🚧 Tick mark positioning improvements
- 🚧 Additional customization options (tick formatting, axis configuration)

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### Bars Not Showing [#bars-not-showing]

If bars are not visible:

1. **Check data**: Ensure `series` array has data and `xAccessor`/`yAccessor` return valid values
2. **Check domains**: Verify `yDomain` (if set) includes your data values
3. **Check dimensions**: Ensure container has non-zero width and height

### Tooltip Positioning Issues [#tooltip-positioning-issues]

If tooltips appear in the wrong location:

1. **Check scroll position**: The component accounts for horizontal scroll automatically
2. **Check container**: Ensure the chart container is not transformed or positioned in a complex layout
3. **Verify event targets**: Tooltips use mouse event coordinates and bar group positions

### Performance Issues [#performance-issues]

For better performance:

1. **Limit data points**: Consider pagination or filtering for very large datasets (>100 points)
2. **Debounce resize**: The default 15ms debounce on `useParentSize` balances smoothness and performance
3. **Simplify tooltips**: If tooltips are complex, consider using simpler content or disabling them

## Props [#props]

### BarChart [#barchart]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />

# Gauge Chart

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### Gauge Not Sizing Correctly [#gauge-not-sizing-correctly]

The component uses `container-type: inline-size` and fills its parent width. Ensure the parent has a defined width:

```tsx
// ❌ No width constraint — gauge may stretch to full viewport
<GaugeChart label="50%" value={50} aria-label="Progress" />

// ✅ Parent provides width context
<div style={{ width: 200 }}>
  <GaugeChart label="50%" value={50} aria-label="Progress" />
</div>

// ✅ Or use className for max-width
<GaugeChart className="my-gauge" label="50%" value={50} aria-label="Progress" />
```

### Value Out of Range [#value-out-of-range]

Values outside the valid range are clamped silently at runtime. For continuous mode the range is 0–100; for segmented mode the range is 0 to the segment count.

```tsx
// ✅ Continuous: 0–100
<GaugeChart label="75%" value={75} aria-label="Score" />

// ✅ Segmented: 0 to segments
<GaugeChart label="3/5" value={3} segments={5} aria-label="Risk level" />
```

## Props [#props]

### GaugeChart [#gaugechart]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />


# LineChart

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Customization [#customization]

### Data Attributes [#data-attributes]

The chart root exposes data attributes that reflect prop state for styling:

**Chart container:** `data-width`, `data-height`, `data-x-labels`, `data-y-labels`, `data-x-labels-vertical`, `data-x-baseline`, `data-y-baseline`, `data-x-tick-marks`, `data-y-tick-marks`

### Component Customization [#component-customization]

Use the `className` prop on the chart container to add or override styles:

```tsx
<LineChart series={series} className="my-custom-chart" />
```

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### ARIA Support [#aria-support]

- Provide **`aria-label`** to describe the chart (e.g. "Monthly sales revenue from January to May 2024").
- Use **`desc`** for a longer description rendered in the SVG `<desc>` for screen readers.
- The component sets ARIA attributes on interactive and structural elements as needed.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

### When to Use LineChart [#when-to-use-linechart]

- Use for trends over time or along a continuous scale.
- Use when comparing a few series (e.g. 2-5 lines); avoid too many overlapping lines.
- Prefer a single chart with a legend over multiple small charts when comparing the same X range.

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### Chart Not Sizing or Empty [#chart-not-sizing-or-empty]

Ensure the chart has a non-zero size. Place it in a container with explicit dimensions or use `width` and `height`:

```tsx
// ✅ Container with size
<div style={{ width: '100%', height: 400 }}>
  <LineChart series={series} />
</div>

// ✅ Or fixed dimensions on the component
<LineChart series={series} width={600} height={400} />
```

### Dates Not Displaying Correctly [#dates-not-displaying-correctly]

Use `xType="time"` when the X-axis values are Date objects:

```tsx
// ❌ Without xType="time", Date objects may not scale correctly
<LineChart series={seriesWithDates} />

// ✅ Use time scale for Date X values
<LineChart series={seriesWithDates} xType="time" />
```

### Tooltip or Crosshair Not Showing [#tooltip-or-crosshair-not-showing]

Ensure `tooltip`, `showCrosshair`, or `showDataPoints` are not set to `false`, and that the chart receives pointer events (e.g. no overlay blocking hover).

## Props [#props]

### LineChart [#linechart]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />


# Checkbox

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Customization [#customization]

`CheckboxGroup` is composed: write `Label`, a `Group` holding the `Checkbox` items, `Text slot="description"`, and `FieldError`. The `Group` takes its axis, gap, and presentational role from the group's `orientation`, so a bare `<Group>` is all you need; pass your own `direction`/`gap` to lay the items out differently. Each `Checkbox` takes label text next to the indicator.

### Data Attributes [#data-attributes]

Components automatically add data attributes for styling different states:

**CheckboxGroup Container:** `data-invalid`, `data-disabled`, `data-required`, `data-readonly`, `data-orientation`

**Checkbox:** `data-selected`, `data-indeterminate`, `data-hovered`, `data-pressed`, `data-focused`, `data-disabled`

```css
.my-checkbox-group [data-selected] {
  color: #09757a;
  font-weight: 500;
}

.my-checkbox-group[data-invalid] {
  border-color: #db1802;
}

.my-checkbox-group [data-focused] {
  outline: 2px solid #1976d2;
  outline-offset: 2px;
}

.my-checkbox-group [data-indeterminate] {
  background-color: #1976d2;
}

.my-checkbox-group [data-disabled] {
  opacity: 0.4;
  cursor: not-allowed;
}
```

### Component Customization [#component-customization]

Pass `className` or `style` to customize a checkbox field container. Use descendant data-attribute selectors to style the interactive checkbox state:

```jsx
<CheckboxGroup className="custom-checkbox-group">
  <Label>Select options</Label>
  <Group>
    <Checkbox value="option1" className="custom-checkbox">
      Option 1
    </Checkbox>
    <Checkbox value="option2" className="highlighted-checkbox">
      Option 2
    </Checkbox>
  </Group>
</CheckboxGroup>
```

## Key Features [#key-features]

### Indeterminate State [#indeterminate-state]

The `isIndeterminate` prop displays a minus icon to represent a partial selection state. This is useful for "select all" checkboxes when only some items in a collection are selected.

```jsx
<Checkbox isIndeterminate onChange={handleSelectAll}>
  Select All
</Checkbox>
```

### Group Validation [#group-validation]

CheckboxGroup supports validation states and error messages:

- **isRequired**: Marks the group as required with visual indicator
- **isInvalid**: Shows error state styling
- **`FieldError`**: Displays validation error text below the group

```jsx
<CheckboxGroup isRequired isInvalid={!hasSelection}>
  <Label>Required selection</Label>
  <Checkbox value="a">Option A</Checkbox>
  <Checkbox value="b">Option B</Checkbox>
  <FieldError>At least one option must be selected</FieldError>
</CheckboxGroup>
```

### Orientation [#orientation]

Use `orientation="vertical"` (default) to stack checkboxes, or `orientation="horizontal"` to arrange them in a row.

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard Navigation [#keyboard-navigation]

- **Tab**: Moves focus to the next/previous checkbox
- **Space**: Toggles the focused checkbox
- **Shift + Tab**: Moves focus to the previous checkbox

### ARIA Support [#aria-support]

- `aria-disabled` for disabled checkboxes
- `aria-required` when selection is required
- `aria-invalid` for validation errors
- Proper labeling with `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby`

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### Selection Not Updating [#selection-not-updating]

```jsx
// ❌ Wrong: Using both value and defaultValue
<CheckboxGroup value={value} defaultValue={["a"]}>
  <Label>Options</Label>
  <Checkbox value="a">Option A</Checkbox>
</CheckboxGroup>

// ✅ Controlled mode
<CheckboxGroup value={value} onChange={setValue}>
  <Label>Options</Label>
  <Checkbox value="a">Option A</Checkbox>
</CheckboxGroup>

// ✅ Uncontrolled mode
<CheckboxGroup defaultValue={["a"]}>
  <Label>Options</Label>
  <Checkbox value="a">Option A</Checkbox>
</CheckboxGroup>
```

### Indeterminate State Not Updating [#indeterminate-state-not-updating]

The `isIndeterminate` prop must be explicitly managed - it doesn't automatically reflect parent-child relationships:

```jsx
// ✅ Correct: Manually manage indeterminate state
const [childSelections, setChildSelections] = React.useState([]);
const allSelected = childSelections.length === totalChildren;
const someSelected = childSelections.length > 0 && !allSelected;

<Checkbox
  isSelected={allSelected}
  isIndeterminate={someSelected}
  onChange={handleSelectAll}
>
  Select All
</Checkbox>
```

### Styling Overrides Not Applying [#styling-overrides-not-applying]

```css
/* ❌ May not have enough specificity */
.my-custom-checkbox {
  color: red;
}

/* ✅ Use data attributes with className for higher specificity */
.my-checkbox-group [data-selected] {
  color: red;
  font-weight: 600;
}
```

### Keyboard Navigation Not Working [#keyboard-navigation-not-working]

```css
/* ❌ Don't remove focus outlines without replacement */
[data-focused] {
  outline: none;
}

/* ✅ Provide visible focus indicator */
.my-checkbox-group [data-focused] {
  outline: 2px solid #1976d2;
  outline-offset: 2px;
}
```

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

### When to Use Checkboxes [#when-to-use-checkboxes]

- ✅ For selecting multiple independent options
- ✅ When users can select zero, one, or many items
- ✅ For toggling settings or features on/off
- ✅ When all available options should be visible
- ❌ For mutually exclusive options (use Radio instead)
- ❌ For simple on/off toggles without labels (use Toggle/Switch instead)

### Label Guidelines [#label-guidelines]

- Use clear, concise labels that describe what selecting the option means
- Keep labels short (1-5 words when possible)
- Ensure labels are descriptive without being verbose
- Place the most commonly selected options first in groups

### Validation [#validation]

Always provide clear error messages and use appropriate validation states:

```jsx
<CheckboxGroup isRequired isInvalid={!agreedToTerms}>
  <Label>Terms and conditions</Label>
  <Checkbox value="terms">I agree to the terms and conditions</Checkbox>
  <Checkbox value="privacy">I agree to the privacy policy</Checkbox>
  <FieldError>You must agree to the terms to continue</FieldError>
</CheckboxGroup>
```

### Group Organization [#group-organization]

- Limit checkbox groups to 7-10 options for better usability
- Use logical ordering (alphabetical, frequency of use, or importance)
- Consider using CheckboxGroup for related options, even if there are only 2-3
- Provide a group label that clearly describes the choice being made

## Props [#props]

```tsx
<CheckboxGroup>
  <Label />
  <Group>
    <Checkbox />
  </Group>
  <Text slot="description" />
  <FieldError />
</CheckboxGroup>
```

### Checkbox [#checkbox]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />

### CheckboxGroup [#checkboxgroup]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.GroupProps} />

### CheckboxIndicator [#checkboxindicator]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.CheckboxIndicatorProps} />


# Chip

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- `ChipGroup` + `ChipList` + `Chip` for grouped values, selection, keyboard navigation, and removal
- Toggle Chips for selecting multiple peer filters
- Removable Chips for user-added filters and input tokens
- Shared `sm`, `md`, and `lg` sizes, with optional leading icons
- `ChipButton` for menu filters and other actions with a Chip-like appearance

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install @godaddy/antares
```

## Quick start [#quick-start]

```tsx
import { Chip, ChipGroup, ChipList, Label } from '@godaddy/antares';

<ChipGroup>
  <Label>Location</Label>
  <ChipList>
    <Chip id="austin">Austin</Chip>
    <Chip id="chicago">Chicago</Chip>
    <Chip id="denver">Denver</Chip>
  </ChipList>
</ChipGroup>
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Customization [#customization]

### Content [#content]

Use a string for a simple label. For icons or other composed content, wrap the
visible label in `Text` and provide `textValue` for the accessible name. See
**Toggle Chips** and **Removable Chips** above.

### Selection and removal [#selection-and-removal]

`ChipGroup` owns selection and removal behavior. Use a Chip render prop for
state-dependent content, and `Button` with `slot="remove"` together with
`onRemove` for removable items. See **Toggle Chips** and **Removable Chips**.

### Layout and sizing [#layout-and-sizing]

Set `size` on `ChipGroup` to keep a collection consistent. `ChipList` wraps by
default and accepts layout props for custom arrangements. See **Sizes**.

### Button composition [#button-composition]

Use `ChipButton` when Chip presentation is needed without collection semantics.
Compose it with components such as `MenuTrigger`; those components continue to
own open state, focus, and keyboard behavior. See **Menu filter trigger**.

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

- Use `Label` or `aria-label` to name the `ChipGroup`; this names the collection,
  not its individual Chips.
- Give each Chip a visible label, `textValue`, or `aria-label`. Use `textValue`
  when a Chip contains icons, composed content, or a render prop.
- Use a descriptive group label so removal actions can be announced clearly.
- Keep the visible label and the accessible value synchronized.
- `ChipButton` is a real button and exposes menu state through `MenuTrigger`; provide an accessible name when the visible content is incomplete.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Keep labels concise and let them truncate only when the available width requires it.
- Prefer groups of three or more related values.
- Keep one size per group.
- Let `ChipList` wrap instead of forcing a single horizontal line.
- Use removable Chips for user-added filters and tokens.
- For menu filters, use `ChipButton` with `MenuTrigger` and provide the chevron explicitly.

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### A ChipGroup has no accessible name [#a-chipgroup-has-no-accessible-name]

Add a visible `Label` to the group or provide `aria-label`. For an individual Chip
with composed content, provide a visible label, `textValue`, or `aria-label`.

### The remove action does not update the UI [#the-remove-action-does-not-update-the-ui]

Add `onRemove` to `ChipGroup` and remove the returned keys from the collection
owned by your application.

### A composed label is not truncating correctly [#a-composed-label-is-not-truncating-correctly]

Keep the label in `Text`, preserve `textValue`, and constrain the available width
of the surrounding layout. Truncation is visual; the complete accessible value
should remain available.

### The menu trigger does not look like a Chip [#the-menu-trigger-does-not-look-like-a-chip]

Use `ChipButton` inside `MenuTrigger`, include the visible value, and add a
trailing chevron to communicate that the control opens a menu.

## Props [#props]

```tsx
<ChipGroup>
  <Label />
  <ChipList>
    <Chip>
      <Icon />
      <Text />
      <Button slot="remove" />
    </Chip>
  </ChipList>
  <Text slot="description" />
  <Text slot="errorMessage" />
</ChipGroup>
```

For a menu trigger, the button and menu are composed as siblings inside
`MenuTrigger`:

```tsx
<MenuTrigger>
  <ChipButton>
    <Text />
    <Icon />
  </ChipButton>
  <Menu>
    <MenuItem />
    {/* ... */}
  </Menu>
</MenuTrigger>
```

<ArgTypes of={Stories.ChipGroupProps} />

### ChipList [#chiplist]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.ChipListProps} />

### ChipButton [#chipbutton]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.ChipButtonProps} />


# CircularProgress

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### ARIA Support [#aria-support]

- `role="progressbar"` on the container
- `aria-valuenow` is omitted while indeterminate; otherwise it reflects the current value (clamped to 0–100)
- `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` define the range (default `0`–`100`)
- `aria-valuetext` and visible value text are omitted while indeterminate; otherwise `aria-valuetext` provides a formatted string (e.g. `"60%"`) via `Intl.NumberFormat`; the same string is rendered inside the circle. Override the text with the `aria-valuetext` prop, or control formatting with `formatOptions`
- `aria-labelledby` associates the visible label when the `label` prop is provided
- `aria-describedby` wires the `helperText` to the progressbar for screen readers
- The decorative SVG and output text are hidden via `aria-hidden="true"`

## Props [#props]

### CircularProgress [#circularprogress]

# Collapsible

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- Independent sections with controlled or uncontrolled expansion.
- Composed headings, optional status icons, and flexible panel content.
- Persistent panel content when collapsed.
- Accessible keyboard interaction and button-to-panel relationships powered by React Aria Components.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Customization [#customization]

Place a `Heading` containing `Button slot="trigger"` inside Collapsible, followed by CollapsiblePanel.
Add an `Icon slot="indicator"` inside the button for the expansion indicator. The panel accepts text,
links, forms, and other components.

CollapsiblePanel provides the content spacing automatically. Use `contentProps` to customize its
inner container with Box spacing props, a class name, or styles:

```tsx
<CollapsiblePanel contentProps={{ padding: 'sm' }}>
  Additional information.
</CollapsiblePanel>
```

Use `contentProps={{ padding: '0' }}` for content without padding. Props supplied directly to
CollapsiblePanel, including `className`, `style`, and `ref`, apply to the outer panel.

Use `defaultExpanded` for initial expansion, or `isExpanded` with `onExpandedChange` for controlled
state. The callback receives a boolean. Use the Accordion component to coordinate several sections;
in that composition, manage expansion through the group.

Use `className` and `style` to customize each component. Button supports string or state-based
`className` values. Components expose these data attributes for state-based styling:

- `Collapsible`: `data-expanded`, `data-disabled`, and `data-focus-visible-within`.
- Trigger `Button`: `data-hovered`, `data-pressed`, `data-focus-visible`, and `data-disabled`.
- `CollapsiblePanel`: `data-focus-visible-within`.

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard [#keyboard]

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` / `Shift + Tab` | Move between the enabled trigger and controls in the expanded panel |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Toggle the section; focus stays on the trigger |

### ARIA [#aria]

- `Button slot="trigger"` renders a native button with `aria-expanded` for its open state and
  `aria-controls` linked to the panel automatically.
- `CollapsiblePanel` is labeled by its trigger through `aria-labelledby` automatically.
- `CollapsiblePanel` uses `role="group"` by default. Keep it when the panel's content does not need
  a navigation landmark; there is no need to set it explicitly.
- Set `role="region"` on `CollapsiblePanel` when its content warrants a named landmark
  for direct screen-reader navigation.
- Collapsed content stays mounted but is excluded from keyboard and screen-reader navigation.
- `Icon slot="indicator"` is decorative and receives `aria-hidden="true"` automatically.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Use descriptive section titles and keep essential information visible.
- Choose heading levels that fit the page hierarchy and avoid deeply nested sections.
- Include text for status icons so their meaning is available to screen readers.
- Put links, forms, and actions inside the panel.
- Open the panel before moving focus to an input that needs attention.

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### Controlled State Not Updating [#controlled-state-not-updating]

Update `isExpanded` from `onExpandedChange`. Changing `defaultExpanded` after mounting does not
control expansion. Inside Accordion, update the group's `expandedKeys` instead.

### Trigger Not Expanding the Panel [#trigger-not-expanding-the-panel]

Place `Button slot="trigger"` inside the section's Heading. A Button without that slot acts
independently and does not toggle the section.

### Input Values Persist After Closing [#input-values-persist-after-closing]

Panel content stays mounted when collapsed. Reset form state explicitly when the application requires it.

## Props [#props]

```tsx
<Collapsible>
  <Heading>
    <Button slot="trigger">
      <Text />
      <Icon slot="indicator" />
    </Button>
  </Heading>
  <CollapsiblePanel>{/* ... */}</CollapsiblePanel>
</Collapsible>;
```

### Collapsible [#collapsible]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />

### CollapsiblePanel [#collapsiblepanel]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.CollapsiblePanelProps} />


# DatePicker

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- **Composable interior**: Compose `Label`, a `Button slot="trigger"`, `DatePickerCalendar`, and optional `Text` / `FieldError`. Nothing is added for you, and what you write keeps the order you wrote it in. `children` also accepts a function for picker state
- **Trigger and calendar**: An empty `Button slot="trigger"` renders a calendar icon and the formatted value from the field. `DatePickerCalendar` (and `DateRangePickerCalendar`) opens a responsive calendar: it takes `Calendar` props plus `popoverProps` and `drawerProps` for its overlay. Write `Popover`, `Content`, and `Calendar` yourself to replace the whole overlay
- **Sizes**: Each picker is a `SizeProvider`. `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) sets its label, trigger, description, error, and the calendar it opens; without it, the picker follows the surrounding scope
- `DatePicker` (single) and `DateRangePicker` (range): a read-only formatted date label; the whole field opens a calendar
- Built on React Aria - native form integration, validation, focus management, and screen-reader support
- Label formatting via `formatOptions` / `placeholder` on the picker itself, or on `DatePickerValue` / `DateRangePickerValue` in a trigger you write
- `minValue` / `maxValue` bounds and `isDateUnavailable` per-day disabling

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install @godaddy/antares
```

## Working with dates [#working-with-dates]

Values are `CalendarDate` objects. Import the date primitives you need from the `@godaddy/antares/date` subpath:

```tsx
import { parseDate } from '@godaddy/antares/date';
import { DatePicker, Label } from '@godaddy/antares';

function EventDatePicker() {
  return (
    <DatePicker defaultValue={parseDate('2024-03-15')}>
      <Label>Event date</Label>
    </DatePicker>
  );
}
```

Import date helpers from `@godaddy/antares/date` (a re-export of
[`@internationalized/date`](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/internationalized/date/)).
Wrap the app in `<I18nProvider>` so formatting and the calendar follow the user's locale.

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Mobile [#mobile-1]

Below `40rem`, `DatePickerCalendar` and `DateRangePickerCalendar` open a bottom drawer with vertically
scrolling months. Each drawer page contains three months by default. Use Previous/Next to change pages,
choose a month, or type a year to jump directly. The initial date follows `focusedValue`,
`defaultFocusedValue`, the selected date (range start), then today, constrained by the date bounds.

The overlay keeps its container until it closes, including during resizing. Its next opening uses the
current viewport. An initially open server-rendered picker keeps its popover through hydration.

- Set `overlay="popover"` on the calendar to always use the desktop presentation.
- Use `drawerProps` for drawer presentation, such as `maxSize` or an accessible label. It defaults to
  `85dvh`. Open state stays on the picker; `popoverProps` configures the popover.
- `pageCount` sets the number of months in either presentation. Defaults: three in the drawer, one in a
  single-date popover, and two in a range popover. Scrolling stays within the current page. Navigation
  advances by a full page, or by one month with `pageBehavior="single"`.
- Range selection and endpoint dragging follow React Aria. Drawers default to `commitBehavior="reset"`:
  a calendar background press, focus leaving the calendar, or backdrop dismissal cancels a pending
  range and preserves the previous value. Popovers default to `commitBehavior="select"`, which commits
  the pending range on background press or blur. Set `commitBehavior` on `DateRangePickerCalendar` to
  override either default. Escape from a date cell cancels the pending selection.
- `shouldCloseOnSelect={false}` on the picker keeps either presentation open after a selection.

```tsx
<DatePicker>
  <Label>Event date</Label>
  <Button slot="trigger" />
  <DatePickerCalendar drawerProps={{ maxSize: '90dvh' }} />
</DatePicker>
```

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

The drawer has the same accessible name as the picker. Escape, an outside press, or the screen-reader
dismiss control closes it and returns focus to the trigger. Arrow keys and Page Up/Down retain React
Aria's calendar navigation. Scrolling does not move keyboard focus or change the selected value. The
month/year controls follow the focused date, and each grid has its own month heading. Weekday
labels shorten when the calendar has limited space, including with enlarged text. The weekday row is
decorative; each date cell provides its full accessible name.


## Props [#props]

```tsx
<DatePicker>
  <Label />
  <Group>
    <Button slot="trigger">
      <DatePickerValue />
    </Button>
  </Group>
  <Text slot="description" />
  <Popover>
    <Content>
      <Calendar />
    </Content>
  </Popover>
  <FieldError />
</DatePicker>
```

```tsx
<DateRangePicker>
  <Label />
  <Group>
    <Button slot="trigger">
      <DateRangePickerValue />
    </Button>
  </Group>
  <Text slot="description" />
  <Popover>
    <Content>
      <RangeCalendar />
    </Content>
  </Popover>
  <FieldError />
</DateRangePicker>
```

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />

### DateRangePicker [#daterangepicker]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.DateRangePickerProps} />

### DatePickerCalendar [#datepickercalendar]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.DatePickerCalendarProps} />

### DateRangePickerCalendar [#daterangepickercalendar]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.DateRangePickerCalendarProps} />

### DatePickerValue [#datepickervalue]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.DatePickerValueProps} />

### DateRangePickerValue [#daterangepickervalue]

# Drawer

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

An overlay panel that slides in from a screen edge. Built on the same RAC stack as `Modal` (a
modal overlay with an `elevation="overlay"` panel and CSS transitions), it supports sidebar
navigation and bottom sheets.

`DrawerTrigger` wraps a trigger button and a `<Drawer>`, handling open
state automatically.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard [#keyboard]

| Key      | Action                                                |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `Escape` | Close the drawer (unless `isKeyboardDismissDisabled`) |
| `Tab`    | Move focus within the drawer (focus is trapped)       |

### ARIA [#aria]

- `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal="true"` on the drawer panel (via RAC Modal)
- A `Heading slot="title"` labels the dialog via `aria-labelledby`; otherwise pass `aria-label`

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Provide a `Heading slot="title"` or an `aria-label` so the dialog has an accessible name.
- Use `isDismissable` to allow closing via backdrop click.
- Don't nest drawers.

## Props [#props]

```tsx
<Drawer placement="right">
  <Header>
    <Heading slot="title" />
    <CloseButton />
  </Header>
  <Content />
  {/* ... */}
</Drawer>
```

# DropZone

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Blocks [#blocks]

<BlockLink id="project-inquiry-form" />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard [#keyboard]

| Key | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves focus to the drop zone |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Opens the file picker so files can be selected without a pointer |

### Screen readers [#screen-readers]

The drop zone renders a visually hidden `<button>` inside the container. Assistive technology discovers and announces this button as an interactive element — activating it opens the native file picker without a pointer.

The button's accessible name is built from two sources, combined in order:

1. **`<Text slot="label">`** — any `Text` child with `slot="label"` has its `id` linked to the button via `aria-labelledby`. This is the recommended way to provide a contextual label that is also visible to sighted users.
2. **`aria-label`** — pass `aria-label` on the `DropZone` component to override or supplement the label (e.g. `aria-label="Upload profile photo"`). When no `Text slot="label"` is present and no `aria-label` is set, the button falls back to the default "DropZone" label provided by React Aria.

```tsx
<DropZone onDrop={handleDrop}>
  <Text slot="label">Drop files to upload.</Text>
</DropZone>
```

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Use the drop zone alongside a button-based file picker — drag-and-drop is a convenience, never the only way to upload.
- Replace the default text with `children` to communicate the accepted file types and size limits up front.
- Let the drop zone fill its container; constrain it with the surrounding layout rather than setting a fixed width on the component itself.
- Reflect upload state (validating, uploading, error) outside the drop zone so the target area stays clear and predictable.

## Props [#props]

### DropZone [#dropzone]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />

# FileTrigger

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- Turns any pressable component (such as an Antares `Button`) into a file picker trigger.
- Renders a visually hidden `<input type="file">` — no styling of its own.
- Restricts selection by MIME type, allows multiple files, directory selection, and camera capture.
- Resets the input value before every open, so re-selecting the same file still fires `onSelect`.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

`FileTrigger` adds no visuals or ARIA of its own — accessibility comes from the pressable child you provide. Use a component with an accessible name (e.g. an Antares `Button` with clear label text) so assistive technology announces the action. The underlying `<input>` is visually hidden but remains operable by keyboard through the child's press behavior.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- `acceptedFileTypes` is a best-effort filter for the OS picker — always validate file type and size again in your `onSelect` handler, since it can be bypassed.
- Pair `FileTrigger` with `DropZone` to offer both click-to-browse and drag-and-drop. See the DropZone "File Upload" example.
- Keep the child a single pressable element; `FileTrigger` forwards press behavior to whatever you nest inside it.

## Props [#props]

### FileTrigger [#filetrigger]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />


# Heading

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- Renders `h1`-`h6` from the `level` prop (default `3`). The level never changes the visual size.
- Without `size`, takes the heading tier of the surrounding `SizeProvider`.
  `size` picks a step on the heading ramp (`xs` to `2xl`).
- `emphasis` picks a feedback color and changes only the color.
- `slot="title"` inside a `Modal` or `Dialog` sets the accessible name, and takes the overlay's
  title tier, one step above the heading tier.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Props [#props]

### Heading [#heading]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />


# Icon

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

The `Icon` component provides a flexible and performant way to display SVG icons with extensive customization options. Built on top of the Bento Icon system, it features on-demand loading from a CDN, automatic caching, and enhanced props for the Antares design system.

## Features [#features]

- **On-demand loading**: Icons are loaded asynchronously from CDN only when needed
- **Automatic caching**: Once loaded, icons are cached for optimal performance
- **Flexible sizing**: Support for `width` and `height` props
- **Color inheritance**: Uses `currentColor` by default for seamless theme integration
- **Accessibility ready**: Built-in support for screen readers and keyboard navigation
- **TypeScript support**: Fully typed with comprehensive prop interfaces
- **Bento integration**: Extends Bento Icon with additional Antares-specific features

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Props [#props]

### Icon [#icon]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />

### Prop Inheritance [#prop-inheritance]

The component extends `BentoIconProps` and passes through all standard HTML attributes and accessibility props to the underlying Bento Icon component. This includes:

- **Accessibility**: `aria-label`, `aria-describedby`, `role`, `title`
- **Events**: `onClick`, `onMouseOver`, `onFocus`, etc.
- **Styling**: `className`, `style`, `data-*` attributes
- **Transform**: `rotate`, `flip` for icon transformations

## Basic Usage [#basic-usage]

<Story of={Stories.Icon} inline />
<Source language='tsx' code={SourceIcon} />

## Size Variants [#size-variants]

Specify explicit width and height values:

```jsx
<Icon icon="star" width={24} height={24} />
```

You can use different values for width and height:

```jsx
<Icon icon="star" width={32} height={16} />
```

## Customization [#customization]

### Slots [#slots]

The Icon component uses Bento's slot system with the following component hierarchy and available slot override points:

#### Component Hierarchy [#component-hierarchy]

```text
Icon (registered as "Icon")
└── BentoIcon (registered as "BentoIcon", slot="icon")
    └── BentoIllustration (registered as "BentoIllustration", slot="content")
```

#### Available Slot Overrides [#available-slot-overrides]

- **`icon`**: Overrides the entire BentoIcon component - affects icon loading, caching, sprite/SVG mode switching, data attributes, and the overall icon wrapper
- **`icon.content`**: Overrides the BentoIllustration component - affects SVG transformations (rotate, flip), accessibility attributes (`role`, `focusable`, `aria-labelledby`), viewBox calculations, and final SVG element rendering

For complete slot override patterns and examples, see the `@bento/slots` package documentation.

### Custom Icons [#custom-icons]

While the Icon component loads design system approved icons from the CDN by default, teams can introduce custom icons using the underlying Bento Icon system.

#### Adding Icons Synchronously [#adding-icons-synchronously]

Use the `set` method to add custom icons that are available immediately:

```jsx
import { Icon, set, parser } from '@godaddy/antares';

// Add a custom icon from an SVG string
const customIconSvg = '<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="..."/></svg>';

set({
  'custom-logo': parser(customIconSvg),
  'team-icon': (
    <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24">
      <path d="M12 2l3.09 6.26L22 9.27l-5 4.87 1.18 6.88L12 17.77l-6.18 3.25L7 14.14 2 9.27l6.91-1.01L12 2z" />
    </svg>
  )
});

// Now use your custom icon
<Icon icon="custom-logo" />
<Icon icon="team-icon" />
```

#### Adding Icons Asynchronously [#adding-icons-asynchronously]

Use the `ondemand` method to load custom icons from your own sources:

```jsx
import { Icon, ondemand, parser } from '@godaddy/antares';

// Add a custom loader for team-specific icons
const unregister = ondemand(async function loadTeamIcons(iconName) {
  if (iconName.startsWith('team-')) {
    const response = await fetch(`/api/team-icons/${iconName}.svg`);
    const svgContent = await response.text();
    return parser(svgContent);
  }
  // Return undefined to let other loaders handle this icon
});

// Icons prefixed with 'team-' will load from your custom endpoint
<Icon icon="team-dashboard" />
<Icon icon="team-settings" />

// Later, if needed, unregister the loader
unregister();
```

#### Custom Icon APIs [#custom-icon-apis]

The following methods are exported from `@godaddy/antares` for custom icon management:

- **`set(icons)`**: Synchronously add icons to the store
- **`ondemand(loader)`**: Register an asynchronous icon loader (returns unregister function)
- **`parser(svgString)`**: Parse SVG strings into React elements

These are re-exports of the underlying Bento Icon system methods. For complete API documentation, advanced usage patterns, and implementation details, see the `@bento/icon` and `@bento/svg-parser` package documentation.

#### Notes [#notes]

- Custom icons integrate seamlessly with all Icon component features (transformations, accessibility, sprite mode, etc.)
- Multiple `ondemand` loaders can be registered and will be called in order until one returns content
- Use the `parser` function to convert SVG strings to React elements
- Custom icons are cached automatically just like CDN icons

### Styling [#styling]

#### CSS Classes [#css-classes]

The component accepts standard `className` and `style` props:

```jsx
<Icon icon="star" className="my-icon" style={{ margin: '10px' }} />
```

**Important**: When you supply a `className`, you make a commitment to take over all styling of the component as it will remove the standard class names. Use data attributes for targeted styling instead.

#### Data Attributes [#data-attributes]

The component automatically adds data attributes for styling hooks:

- `data-icon`: The icon name (always present)
- `data-color`: Applied when color prop is set
- `data-loading`: Applied during icon loading from CDN
- `data-mode`: Applied when mode prop is set (e.g., "sprite")
- `data-flip`: Applied when flip prop is set ("horizontal" or "vertical")
- `data-rotate`: Applied when rotate prop is set (90, 180, or 270)

The component also includes accessibility attributes:

- `role="presentation"`: For decorative icons
- `role="img"`: When title prop is provided
- `focusable="false"`: Prevents keyboard focus

```css
/* Style by icon name */
[data-icon="star"] {
  color: gold;
}

/* Style by color */
[data-color="red"] {
  border: 1px solid currentColor;
}

/* Style loading state */
[data-loading="true"] {
  opacity: 0.5;
}

/* Style sprite mode */
[data-mode="sprite"] {
  filter: drop-shadow(0 1px 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1));
}

/* Style flipped icons */
[data-flip="horizontal"] {
  transform-origin: center;
}

/* Style rotated icons */
[data-rotate="90"] {
  transition: transform 0.2s ease;
}
```

## Color Customization [#color-customization]

### Inherit from Parent (Default) [#inherit-from-parent-default]

By default, icons inherit the color from their parent element via `currentColor`:

```jsx
<div style={{ color: 'blue' }}>
  <Icon icon="star" /> {/* Will be blue */}
</div>
```

### Explicit Colors [#explicit-colors]

Override the color with specific values:

```jsx
<Icon icon="star" color="#ff6b35" />          // Hex color
<Icon icon="star" color="rgb(255, 107, 53)" /> // RGB color
<Icon icon="star" color="var(--primary-color)" /> // CSS variable
<Icon icon="star" color="currentColor" />     // Explicit inheritance
```

## Icon Transformations [#icon-transformations]

Transform capabilities are inherited from the Bento Illustration component. For complete transformation options and implementation details, see the `@bento/illustration` package documentation.

### Rotation [#rotation]

Rotate icons by 90-degree increments:

```jsx
<Icon icon="arrow" rotate={90} />   // 90 degrees
<Icon icon="arrow" rotate={180} />  // 180 degrees
<Icon icon="arrow" rotate={270} />  // 270 degrees
```

### Flipping [#flipping]

Flip icons horizontally or vertically:

```jsx
<Icon icon="arrow" flip="horizontal" />
<Icon icon="arrow" flip="vertical" />
```

## Loading States [#loading-states]

### Placeholder Content [#placeholder-content]

Provide fallback SVG content while icons load from the CDN:

```jsx
<Icon icon="star">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor">
    <circle cx="12" cy="12" r="3" />
  </svg>
</Icon>
```

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Decorative Icons [#decorative-icons]

For purely decorative icons, no additional attributes are needed. The icon will have `role="presentation"` and be ignored by screen readers:

```jsx
<Icon icon="star" /> {/* Decorative, screen readers will ignore */}
```

### Semantic Icons [#semantic-icons]

For icons that convey meaning, use the `title` prop. This automatically adds `role="img"` and provides screen reader accessible text:

```jsx
{/* Semantic icon - use title prop */}
<Icon icon="star" title="Favorite item" />

{/* Warning icon with semantic meaning */}
<Icon icon="alert" title="Warning: Your session will expire soon" />

{/* Status indicator with meaning */}
<Icon icon="check-circle" title="Task completed successfully" />
```

### Interactive Icons [#interactive-icons]

For interactive icons within buttons or links, use the `title` prop on the icon and `aria-label` on the interactive element:

```jsx
{/* Button with icon - label the button, not the icon */}
<button aria-label="Close dialog">
  <Icon icon="close" />
</button>

{/* Icon button where icon has semantic meaning */}
<button aria-label="Mark as favorite">
  <Icon icon="star" title="Favorite" />
</button>

{/* Link with icon */}
<a href="/settings" aria-label="Go to settings">
  <Icon icon="settings" />
</a>
```

## Performance Considerations [#performance-considerations]

### Default Icon Loading [#default-icon-loading]

Icons are loaded on-demand from a CDN using the following process:

1. **First Request**: When an icon is first encountered, it triggers an asynchronous fetch from the CDN
2. **SVG Parsing**: The fetched SVG string is parsed into a React element using `@bento/svg-parser`
3. **Automatic Caching**: Once loaded, the icon is cached in memory to avoid subsequent network requests
4. **Full SVG Rendering**: Each icon instance renders as a complete SVG element with all path data

```jsx
// Each icon renders as a full SVG element
<Icon icon="star" />  // <svg><path d="M3 22v-20l18 10-18 10z" /></svg>
<Icon icon="star" />  // <svg><path d="M3 22v-20l18 10-18 10z" /></svg>
<Icon icon="star" />  // <svg><path d="M3 22v-20l18 10-18 10z" /></svg>
```

This approach works well for SSR and small numbers of icons, but can lead to DOM bloat when the same icon appears many times.

### Sprite Mode Optimization [#sprite-mode-optimization]

When `mode="sprite"` is enabled, the component switches to a more efficient rendering strategy:

```jsx
<Icon icon="star" mode="sprite" />
<Icon icon="star" mode="sprite" />
<Icon icon="star" mode="sprite" />
```

**What happens with sprite mode:**

1. **Sprite Sheet Creation**: A hidden SVG sprite sheet is automatically injected into the DOM containing symbol definitions
2. **Reference Rendering**: Each icon renders as a lightweight `<use>` element that references the sprite
3. **Deduplication**: Icon path data only exists once in the sprite sheet, regardless of how many times it's used
4. **Client-Side Hydration**: The sprite sheet is generated and injected after hydration, causing a brief paint event

**DOM Output:**

```html
<!-- Hidden sprite sheet (created automatically) -->
<svg id="bento-svg-sprite" style="display: none;">
  <symbol id="bento-svg-spritesheet-star" viewBox="0 0 24 24">
    <path d="M3 22v-20l18 10-18 10z" />
  </symbol>
</svg>

<!-- Lightweight icon references -->
<svg><use xlink:href="#bento-svg-spritesheet-star" /></svg>
<svg><use xlink:href="#bento-svg-spritesheet-star" /></svg>
<svg><use xlink:href="#bento-svg-spritesheet-star" /></svg>
```

**Performance Benefits:**

- **Reduced DOM Size**: Path data stored once instead of duplicated
- **Lower Memory Usage**: Especially beneficial with many repeated icons
- **Faster Rendering**: Browser optimizations for `<use>` elements

**Trade-offs:**

- **SSR Limitation**: Sprite references render empty until client-side hydration
- **Initial Flash**: Brief moment where icons appear/disappear during sprite injection

### Recommendations [#recommendations]

- **Use default mode** for SSR applications or when icons appear infrequently
- **Use sprite mode** when the same icons appear many times (navigation, lists, tables)
- **Consider preloading** frequently used icons to reduce loading delays
- **Provide fallback content** for critical icons to handle loading states

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### Icon Not Loading [#icon-not-loading]

If an icon fails to load:

1. **Check icon name**: Ensure the icon exists in the CDN
2. **Network connectivity**: Verify CDN is accessible
3. **Check browser console**: Look for network errors
4. **Fallback content**: Provide placeholder content for loading states

### Performance Issues [#performance-issues]

For performance optimization:

1. **Preload common icons**: Consider preloading frequently used icons
2. **Use sprite mode**: For repeated icons, consider sprite mode which consolidates multiple icons into a single SVG sprite sheet, reducing DOM size and improving performance when the same icon appears multiple times
3. **Minimize icon sets**: Only load icons that are actually used

# InlineDrawer

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

`InlineDrawerPanel` is the collapsible content for the accordion pattern — a thin wrapper over RAC `DisclosurePanel` that hides when collapsed. The trigger is any component you slot in with `slot="trigger"` — there's no dedicated trigger component.

## Features [#features]

- In-flow collapsible built on RAC Disclosure — bring your own trigger via `slot="trigger"`
- Animated by default; `animate={false}` disables the transition
- `placement` selects the collapse axis (`left`/`right` → width, `top`/`bottom` → height)
- Controlled and uncontrolled modes (`isExpanded` / `defaultExpanded` / `onExpandedChange`)
- Accordion collapse uses the browser's `hidden="until-found"` for find-in-page
- `prefers-reduced-motion` support

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard [#keyboard]

| Key               | Action                         |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `Enter` / `Space` | Toggle via the slotted trigger |
| `Tab`             | Move focus through the content |

### ARIA [#aria]

- A `<Button slot="trigger">` gets `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls` wired to the `InlineDrawerPanel` automatically (via RAC Disclosure).
- For the sidebar rail, the toggle is your own control (e.g. a `ToggleButton`) — give icon-only buttons an `aria-label`, and the content stays in the DOM and accessible since nothing is hidden.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Accordion → `Button slot="trigger"` + `InlineDrawerPanel`. Sidebar rail → controlled state + always-visible children.
- For the rail, use numeric (px) `minSize`/`maxSize` so the width animates; `min-content`/`max-content` fit the content exactly but won't animate.
- `placement` does not flip in RTL; the side is decided by document/flex order.
- Don't nest InlineDrawers.

## Props [#props]

```tsx
<InlineDrawer>
  <Button slot="trigger" />
  <InlineDrawerPanel>
    {/* ... */}
  </InlineDrawerPanel>
</InlineDrawer>
```

### InlineDrawer [#inlinedrawer]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />

### InlineDrawerPanel [#inlinedrawerpanel]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.InlineDrawerPanelProps} />

# Box

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

`Box` is a polymorphic layout component that renders as any HTML element or custom component via the `as` prop. It provides consistent spacing, elevation, rounding, and self-alignment within flex or grid containers.

**Important**: Since `Flex` and `Grid` extend `Box`, prefer them for layouts. Use `Box` only when you need a non-flex, non-grid container.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Scale Sizes [#scale-sizes]

The spacing props use semantic t-shirt sizes for padding, gap, and other spacing properties:

- `xs` - Extra small spacing
- `sm` - Small spacing
- `md` - Medium spacing
- `lg` - Large spacing
- `xl` - Extra large spacing
- `2xl` - 2x extra large spacing

Custom CSS values are also supported for edge cases.

## Polymorphic `as` details [#polymorphic-as-details]

**HTML Elements:** When using `as="button"`, TypeScript enforces button-specific props like `type`, `disabled`, and `onClick`.

**Custom Components:** When using `as={MyComponent}`, Box accepts that component's props. If there's a prop name conflict, Box's props take priority.

**Typed Refs:** Refs are correctly typed based on the `as` value - `useRef<HTMLButtonElement>` works with `as="button"`.

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## RTL Support [#rtl-support]

Box uses CSS logical properties (`padding-inline-start`, `padding-block-end`, etc.) which automatically adapt to RTL layouts. No additional configuration is needed.

## Design Tokens [#design-tokens]

All spacing, elevation, and rounding values are derived from the theme. If no theme is provided, default values are used. This ensures consistency across the design system.

## Context and slots [#context-and-slots]

`BoxContext` supplies default props to Boxes in its subtree. A `slots` map supplies defaults to
named parts; each Box selects one with `slot`. Explicit consumer props override defaults, while
classes, styles, and refs are merged. Pass `slot={null}` to opt out of the context.

```tsx
<BoxContext.Provider value={{ slots: { content: { padding: 'md', className: 'content' } } }}>
  <Box slot="content">Content</Box>
</BoxContext.Provider>
```

Flex and Grid render through Box and also consume BoxContext. Named slot maps require a matching
slot unless the provider includes an unslotted default. Nested providers replace the outer context.

## Props [#props]

### Box [#box]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />


# Flex

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

`Flex` is a one-dimensional layout component for arranging children in rows or columns with alignment and spacing control. It extends `Box`, inheriting all `Box` capabilities (padding, elevation, rounding, self-alignment, and polymorphic `as` prop).

**Recommended default**: Use `Flex` for most layouts. Since it extends `Box`, you get all `Box` capabilities without needing to nest components.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Scale Sizes [#scale-sizes]

We use the same scale sizes as the `Box` component.

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## RTL Support [#rtl-support]

Flex uses CSS logical properties which automatically adapt to RTL layouts. The `direction` prop values (`row`, `row-reverse`) respect the document direction.

## Design Tokens [#design-tokens]

All gap and padding values are derived from the theme. If no theme is provided, default values are used. This ensures consistency across the design system.

## Migration from @ux/box [#migration-from-uxbox]

| Current `@ux/box`                    | New Pattern                      |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- |
| `<Box orientation="horizontal">`     | `<Flex direction="row" >`        |
| `<Box orientation="vertical">`       | `<Flex direction="column" >`     |
| `<Box blockAlignChildren="center">`  | `<Flex justifyContent="center">` |
| `<Box inlineAlignChildren="center">` | `<Flex alignItems="center">`     |

## Props [#props]

### Flex [#flex]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />


# Grid

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

`Grid` is a two-dimensional CSS Grid layout component for complex grid-based layouts. It extends `Box`, inheriting all `Box` capabilities (padding, elevation, rounding, self-alignment, and polymorphic `as` prop).

**Use `Grid` when**: You need explicit two-dimensional layouts with rows and columns, named grid areas, or responsive auto-fill patterns.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Scale Sizes [#scale-sizes]

We use the same scale sizes as the `Box` component.

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## RTL Support [#rtl-support]

Grid uses CSS logical properties which automatically adapt to RTL layouts. Grid areas and alignment respect the document direction.

## Grid vs Flex [#grid-vs-flex]

| Use Case                   | Recommended      |
| -------------------------- | ---------------- |
| Single row/column of items | Flex             |
| Two-dimensional layouts    | Grid             |
| Named layout regions       | Grid             |
| Auto-wrapping cards        | Grid (auto-fill) |
| Navigation bars            | Flex             |
| Form layouts               | Grid             |

## Props [#props]

### Grid [#grid]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />


# ListBox

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- **Single or multiple selection**: Set `selectionMode="single"` or `"multiple"`.
- **Controlled or uncontrolled**: Use `selectedKeys` and `onSelectionChange` for controlled state, or `defaultSelectedKeys` for uncontrolled.
- **Layout primitive**: `ListBox` and `ListBoxItem` accept layout props (`gap`, `padding`, etc.) — they extend `FlexOwnProps`.
- **Composes into other components**: `Select` uses `ListBox` internally; reach for `ListBox` directly when you need an inline list rather than a popover dropdown.
- **React Aria integration**: Built on React Aria ListBox for accessibility, keyboard navigation, and typeahead.

`ListBox` requires either `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. For a labeled, popover-style picker, prefer `Select`.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

```tsx
<ListBox>
  <ListBoxItem />
  {/* ... */}
</ListBox>
```
