# Menu

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

An accessible dropdown menu built on React Aria. It supports grouping with optional
titles, multi-select checkbox items, leading icons, submenus, and two sizes. It
reuses Antares' `Popover` for the overlay and `Checkbox` indicator for selection.

## Features [#features]

- Grouping with an optional title via `MenuGroup`, plus `MenuSeparator` dividers
- Multi-select groups: set `selectionMode="multiple"` on a `MenuGroup` to render
  its items as checkboxes, while other groups stay plain action items
- Optional leading `icon` per item; links (`href`) and disabled items
- Submenus via `SubmenuTrigger`
- Two sizes (`sm`, `md`); set `size` explicitly on each submenu `Menu`
- Usable anchored to a trigger or standalone (e.g. inside a bottom-sheet `Drawer`)

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

- **Space/Enter**: activate an item; **Escape**: close
- **Arrow Up/Down**: move between items; **Home/End**: first/last
- **Arrow Right/Left**: open/close a submenu
- **Type to select**: jump to a matching item (string labels are used as `textValue`)
- Multi-select items use RAC's `menuitemcheckbox` role; the checkbox indicator is
  decorative (`aria-hidden`) and the item owns interaction

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Give each selectable `MenuItem` a stable `id`, and provide the `Menu` an
  `aria-label` when there is no visible label.
- Use a leading `icon` for recognition, not as the only label - keep a text label.
- Reserve checkbox groups for multi-select; use plain groups for one-shot actions.
- A `Menu` is a collection: it only renders `MenuItem`, `MenuGroup`,
  `MenuSeparator`, and `SubmenuTrigger`. For rich content (a `Calendar`, a form),
  close the menu from `onAction` and open a separate `Popover` anchored with
  `triggerRef` instead of putting it in a submenu.

## Props [#props]

```tsx
<MenuTrigger>
  <Button />
  <Menu>
    <MenuGroup>
      <MenuItem />
      <MenuSeparator />
    </MenuGroup>
    <SubmenuTrigger>
      <MenuItem />
      <Menu />
    </SubmenuTrigger>
  </Menu>
</MenuTrigger>
```

### Menu [#menu]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />

### MenuTrigger [#menutrigger]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.MenuTriggerProps} />

### MenuGroup [#menugroup]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.MenuGroupProps} />

### MenuItem [#menuitem]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.MenuItemProps} />

### MenuSeparator [#menuseparator]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.MenuSeparatorProps} />

### SubmenuTrigger [#submenutrigger]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.SubmenuTriggerProps} />


# MetricsLockup

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

MetricsLockup displays a metric value prominently, with an optional title and tooltip for context, an optional trend icon to show direction of change, and a description label below the value.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard [#keyboard]

| Key    | Description                                                         |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tab    | Moves focus to the info trigger button and shows the tooltip        |
| Escape | Closes the tooltip                                                  |

### ARIA [#aria]

- The info trigger button uses `aria-label="More information"` to describe its purpose.
- The tooltip uses `role="tooltip"` and is associated with the info trigger via `aria-describedby`.
- The info trigger has a minimum touch target of 44×44px, achieved via a CSS pseudo-element, to meet WCAG 2.5.5.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Keep tooltip content concise and informative.
- The `data` prop accepts strings or numbers — format currency and percentages before passing them in.
- `titleInfo` requires `title` to be set — the info icon is contextually tied to the title label. If `title` is absent, `titleInfo` has no effect.
- `trend` is intended to accompany `description` to provide temporal context (e.g. "↑ +3% vs. last month"). A trend icon alone, with no description, leaves the direction unanchored ("up since *when*?"). If `description` is not provided, `trend` has no effect.

## Props [#props]

### MetricsLockup [#metricslockup]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />


# Modal

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

`ModalTrigger` wraps a trigger button and a `<Modal>`, handling open state automatically. Based on RAC `DialogTrigger`.

The modal is a `SizeProvider`. It opens at the size of the scope around its trigger, even though it renders in a portal, and `size` overrides that.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard interaction [#keyboard-interaction]

| Key      | Action                                                     |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`    | Moves focus to the next focusable element inside the modal |
| `Escape` | Closes the modal (unless `isKeyboardDismissDisabled`)      |

### ARIA [#aria]

- `role="dialog"` is applied automatically by the underlying React Aria `Dialog`
- Focus is trapped within the modal while open and returned to the trigger on close

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Always include a `Heading slot="title"` so the dialog has an accessible name; otherwise pass `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` on `<Modal>`
- Pair every action button with `slot="close"` when it should dismiss the modal
- Set `isDismissable={false}` to prevent outside-click dismissal for required confirmations; to also block `Escape`, pass `isKeyboardDismissDisabled`

## Props [#props]

```tsx
<ModalTrigger>
  <Button />
  <Modal>
    <Heading slot="title" />
    <CloseButton />
    <Header />
    <Content />
    <Footer />
    <ButtonGroup />
    {/* ... */}
  </Modal>
</ModalTrigger>
```

### Modal [#modal]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />

### ModalTrigger [#modaltrigger]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.ModalTriggerProps} />


# NumberField

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- **Composable interior**: Compose `Label`, the control, `Text slot="description"`, and `FieldError`. Nothing is added for you, and what you write keeps the order you wrote it in
- **Steppers**: A stepper is a `Group` holding `Button slot="decrement"`, an `Input`, and `Button slot="increment"`. Left empty, each button takes its icon and `variant="control"` from the field, so no icon imports are needed. Compose a bare `Input` instead for a plain numeric input
- **Sizes**: The field is a `SizeProvider`. `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) sets its label, input, steppers, description, and error; without it, the field follows the surrounding scope
- **Value scale**: `minValue`, `maxValue`, `step`, and `formatOptions` configure the numeric behavior
- **Controlled or uncontrolled**: Use `value` and `onChange` for controlled state, or `defaultValue` for uncontrolled
- **Validation states**: Use `isInvalid` with a `FieldError` and `isDisabled` for validation and disabled state

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Props [#props]

```tsx
<NumberField>
  <Label />
  <Group>
    <Button slot="decrement" />
    <Input />
    <Button slot="increment" />
  </Group>
  {/* or a bare <Input /> for a plain numeric input */}
  <Text slot="description" />
  <FieldError />
</NumberField>
```

### NumberField [#numberfield]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />


# Pagination

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- Controlled and uncontrolled 1-based page state.
- Explicit composition with Antares `Button`, `Input`, `Text`, `Select` and `PaginationDots`.
- Known and unknown page-count data sources.
- React Aria context defaults for previous, next and the single page input.
- Medium and small control sizes.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Customization [#customization]

Pagination is composed: pass only the regions your layout needs. Previous and
next `Button`s and the page `Input` receive navigation defaults from
Pagination, while explicit child props—including disabled-state props—and
`className` values remain available for local customization. Separator, page count,
`Select` and
`PaginationDots` are consumer-owned.

Use `className` to extend styling without replacing the interaction behavior
provided by Antares.

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

- Pagination does not add translated labels. Provide accessible names for the
  navigation region, previous/next buttons and page input.
- `PaginationDots` is decorative and does not replace interactive page
  controls.
- For interactive page links, compose explicit `Button` or `LinkButton` children and
  provide the active state with `aria-current="page"`.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Pass `pageCount` when the backend exposes a known number of pages.
- Omit `pageCount` for cursor-based data and disable the composed next button
  when the backend reports that there is no next page.
- Keep total items, page size and result ranges in the consuming data layer.
- Compose exactly one page `Input`; use a separate component for advanced range
  navigation.

## Props [#props]

### Pagination [#pagination]

```tsx
<Pagination>
  <Button slot="previous" />
  <Input />
  {/* separator, page count, Select, PaginationDots, or custom regions */}
  <Button slot="next" />
</Pagination>
```

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />

### PaginationDots [#paginationdots]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.PaginationDotsProps} />


# Popover

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

`PopoverTrigger` wraps a trigger button and a `<Popover>`, handling open state and positioning automatically.
Based on RAC `DialogTrigger`. To anchor a popover to an element it doesn't wrap, pass `triggerRef` instead.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard [#keyboard]

| Key           | Action                             |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `Enter/Space` | Opens the popover from its trigger |
| `Escape`      | Closes the popover                 |

### ARIA [#aria]

- `role="dialog"` is applied automatically by the underlying React Aria `Dialog`
- A `Heading slot="title"` labels the dialog via `aria-labelledby`. Without one, a popover inside
  a `PopoverTrigger` falls back to being labelled by its trigger; standing alone with
  `triggerRef` it needs an explicit `aria-label`

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Pass an `aria-label` when anchoring with `triggerRef` instead of wrapping a `PopoverTrigger`,
  since there is no trigger to borrow the name from.
- Popover width is determined by its content, and it's recommended to keep it under 400px.

## Props [#props]

```tsx
<PopoverTrigger>
  <Button />
  <Popover>
    <Heading slot="title" />
    <CloseButton />
    <Content />
    {/* ... */}
  </Popover>
</PopoverTrigger>
```

### PopoverTrigger [#popovertrigger]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.PopoverTriggerProps} />


# Pressable

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- Adds accessible press behavior to an existing visual component.
- Applies interaction states directly to the child without adding a wrapper element.
- Supports pointer, touch, and keyboard interactions through React Aria.
- Preserves the child's layout, shape, and base visual styling while adding state feedback.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Customization [#customization]

Use `Pressable` when an existing visual component or layout surface needs press behavior while keeping its own DOM element, layout, and styles. The child must be a single element that forwards its ref and accepts the DOM, ARIA, and event props supplied by React Aria.

Use `Button` when you need a standard button control with button-specific sizing, layout, and visual variants.

Pass `onPress` for the action instead of wiring separate pointer and keyboard handlers:

```tsx
<Pressable aria-label="View account summary" onPress={handlePress}>
  <Box role="button" padding="md" rounding="md" elevation="card">
    Account summary
  </Box>
</Pressable>
```

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

`Pressable` accepts the React Aria press props, including `onPress`, `onPressStart`, `onPressEnd`, `onPressUp`, and `onPressChange`.

Use a semantic interactive element when possible. For a non-semantic child such as `Avatar` or `Box`, provide an appropriate interactive role and an accessible name. Pressable makes the child focusable when the required props are forwarded.

Do not add `role="button"` to a native `<button>` or `<a>` unless you intentionally need to change its semantics. Use a dedicated semantic component such as `Button`, `LinkButton`, `Menu`, or `ToggleButton` when that control's meaning is known.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Prefer a native interactive element or a semantic Antares component when the interaction meaning is known.
- Avoid nesting interactive elements inside the child passed to `Pressable`.
- `Pressable` automatically applies React Aria state attributes such as `[data-hovered]`, `[data-pressed]`, `[data-focus-visible]`, and `[data-disabled]` to the child. Ensure the child component styles these states appropriately if it overrides the default `Pressable` styles.

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

- If React Aria warns that the child must be focusable, ensure it is a single element that forwards its ref, `tabIndex`, DOM props, and ARIA attributes.
- If `onPress` does not fire, confirm that the child forwards event handlers and is not disabled by another component.

## Props [#props]

```tsx
<Pressable>
  <Box />
</Pressable>
```

### Pressable [#pressable]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />

# ProgressSteps

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- Horizontal and vertical orientations
- Four completion statuses (`none`, `partial`, `complete`, `error`) with status icons
- Timeline (past / current / future) derived from a single `currentStep` prop
- Auto-generated step numbers (opt out with `hideStepNumbers`)
- Interactive (navigable) and inert (display-only) steps
- Title truncation and RTL support
- Rendered as a `<nav>` landmark with an ordered list for assistive technology

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Customization [#customization]

- Step numbers (`"N. "`) are prepended automatically — keep them where possible, as user testing shows people recognize the component better with them. Set `hideStepNumbers` to omit them.
- `orientation` switches between `horizontal` (accent bar on top) and `vertical` (accent bar on the leading edge).
- `currentStep` is the single source of truth for the timeline. Omit it for a not-yet-started flow where every step is `future`; pass the step count for a fully completed flow where every step is `past`.
- `status` is independent of timeline and only controls the status icon and (for `error`) the accent bar color.
- Pass `className` to the container or an individual step to extend the styles.

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

- The container renders a `<nav>` landmark; set `aria-label` to name it (defaults to `"Progress"`).
- Steps are an ordered list (`<ol>`/`<li>`) so assistive technology conveys position and count.
- The current step is marked with `aria-current="step"`.
- Interactive steps are real buttons: focusable in the natural **Tab** order and activated with **Enter** or **Space**. Status icons are decorative (`aria-hidden`).
- Focus is shown with a visible outline; disabled steps use `0.4` opacity and are not focusable.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Drive the timeline from `currentStep` rather than styling individual steps.
- Provide `onPress` only for steps a user can actually navigate to; leave it off for display-only steps.
- Keep titles short — they truncate with an ellipsis when space is tight.
- Always give the container an `aria-label` that describes the flow (e.g. `"Checkout progress"`).

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

- **No step is highlighted:** `currentStep` is omitted, negative, or out of range. Set it to the active step's 0-based index.
- **A step isn't clickable:** it has no `onPress`, so it's inert by design. Add `onPress` to make it interactive.
- **Titles overflow:** that's expected — titles truncate. Shorten the title.

## Props [#props]

```tsx
<ProgressSteps>
  <ProgressStep />
  {/* ... */}
</ProgressSteps>
```

### ProgressSteps [#progresssteps]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />

### ProgressStep [#progressstep]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.ProgressStepProps} />


# Radio

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Customization [#customization]

`RadioGroup` is composed: write `Label`, a `Group` holding the `Radio` items, `Text slot="description"`, and `FieldError`. The `Group` takes its axis, gap, and presentational role from the group's `orientation`, so a bare `<Group>` is all you need; pass your own `direction`/`gap` to lay the items out differently. Each `Radio` takes label text next to the indicator. `orientation` also sets keyboard-navigation direction and ARIA.

### Data Attributes [#data-attributes]

Components automatically add data attributes for styling different states:

**RadioGroup Container:** `data-invalid`, `data-disabled`, `data-required`, `data-readonly`, `data-orientation`

**Radio Button:** `data-selected`, `data-hovered`, `data-pressed`, `data-focused`, `data-disabled`

```css
.my-radio-group [data-selected] {
  color: #09757a;
  font-weight: 500;
}

.my-radio-group[data-invalid] {
  border-color: #db1802;
}

.my-radio-group [data-focused] {
  outline: 2px solid #1976d2;
  outline-offset: 2px;
}

.my-radio-group [data-disabled] {
  opacity: 0.4;
  cursor: not-allowed;
}
```

### Component Customization [#component-customization]

Pass `className` or `style` to customize a radio field container. Use descendant data-attribute selectors to style the interactive radio state:

```jsx
<RadioGroup className="custom-radio-group">
  <Label>Select plan</Label>
  <Group>
    <Radio value="basic" className="custom-radio">
      Basic
    </Radio>
    <Radio value="premium" className="premium-radio">
      Premium
    </Radio>
  </Group>
</RadioGroup>
```

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard Navigation [#keyboard-navigation]

- **Tab**: Moves focus to/from the radio group
- **Arrow Down/Right**: Move to next radio button
- **Arrow Up/Left**: Move to previous radio button
- **Space**: Select the focused radio button

### ARIA Support [#aria-support]

- `role="radiogroup"` on the container
- `role="radio"` on each option
- `aria-checked` indicates selection state
- `aria-disabled` for disabled options
- `aria-required` when selection is required
- `aria-invalid` for validation errors

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### Selection Not Updating [#selection-not-updating]

```jsx
// ❌ Wrong: Using both value and defaultValue
<RadioGroup value={value} defaultValue="basic">
  <Label>Plan</Label>
  <Group>
    <Radio value="basic">Basic</Radio>
  </Group>
</RadioGroup>

// ✅ Controlled mode
<RadioGroup value={value} onChange={setValue}>
  <Label>Plan</Label>
  <Group>
    <Radio value="basic">Basic</Radio>
  </Group>
</RadioGroup>

// ✅ Uncontrolled mode
<RadioGroup defaultValue="basic">
  <Label>Plan</Label>
  <Group>
    <Radio value="basic">Basic</Radio>
  </Group>
</RadioGroup>
```

### Styling Overrides Not Applying [#styling-overrides-not-applying]

```css
/* ❌ May not have enough specificity */
.my-custom-radio {
  color: red;
}

/* ✅ Use data attributes and className for higher specificity */
.my-radio-group [data-selected] {
  color: red;
  font-weight: 600;
}
```

### Keyboard Navigation Not Working [#keyboard-navigation-not-working]

```css
/* ❌ Don't remove focus outlines without replacement */
[data-focused] {
  outline: none;
}

/* ✅ Provide visible focus indicator */
.my-radio-group [data-focused] {
  outline: 2px solid #1976d2;
  outline-offset: 2px;
}
```

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

### When to Use Radio Buttons [#when-to-use-radio-buttons]

- ✅ When there are 2-7 mutually exclusive options
- ✅ When all options should be visible at once
- ✅ When the decision is important and deserves space
- ❌ For more than 7 options (use Select instead)
- ❌ For binary yes/no choices (use Checkbox or Toggle instead)
- ❌ When space is limited (use Select dropdown)

### Label Guidelines [#label-guidelines]

- Use clear, concise labels
- Keep labels short (1-3 words when possible)
- Place the most common option first
- Ensure labels are descriptive without being verbose

### Validation [#validation]

Always provide clear error messages:

```jsx
<RadioGroup isRequired isInvalid={!selectedShipping}>
  <Label>Select shipping method</Label>
  <Group>
    <Radio value="standard">Standard</Radio>
    <Radio value="express">Express</Radio>
  </Group>
  <FieldError>Please select a shipping method</FieldError>
</RadioGroup>
```

## Props [#props]

```tsx
<RadioGroup>
  <Label />
  <Group>
    <Radio />
  </Group>
  <Text slot="description" />
  <FieldError />
</RadioGroup>
```

### Radio [#radio]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />

### RadioGroup [#radiogroup]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.GroupProps} />


# RangeField

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- Select one value or render one thumb for each value in an array
- Supports controlled and uncontrolled values with typed change callbacks
- Provides localized value output, endpoint labels, descriptions, and markers
- Integrates with native forms, keyboard, pointer, and touch interaction through React Aria

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Accessible names [#accessible-names]

For a single value, prefer a visible `label`; use `aria-label` only when equivalent visible context already exists.

For an array, provide one descriptive `thumbLabels` entry for every value. Entries are matched by index, so keep them aligned when values are added, removed, or reordered. Describe each thumb's purpose, such as `Lower warning threshold`, rather than its current number.

`thumbNames` configures native form field names and does not provide accessible labels. Likewise, `valueLabel`, `minLabel`, and `maxLabel` are visual context rather than substitutes for accessible naming.

### Keyboard interaction [#keyboard-interaction]

Each thumb follows the React Aria slider keyboard model:

- Tab and Shift+Tab move among thumbs and surrounding controls.
- Arrow Right and Arrow Up increase the focused value by `step`.
- Arrow Left and Arrow Down decrease the focused value by `step`.
- Home and End move the focused thumb to its permitted bounds.
- Page Up and Page Down make larger changes.

Directional behavior follows the user's locale where appropriate. Pointer, touch, and keyboard interaction all use the same scale and constraints.

Markers are decorative and hidden from the accessibility tree. Ensure the field label, thumb labels, bounds, step, and formatted values communicate all required information without relying on marker appearance.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Use an array only when every entry has a clear, independently adjustable meaning.
- Keep `value`, `thumbLabels`, and `thumbNames` aligned by index.
- Use thumb labels that explain purpose instead of repeating the current number.
- Keep array values in a stable semantic order. If crossing or reordering thumbs would make their meaning ambiguous, enforce the appropriate ordering in product state.
- Avoid large value arrays. Every entry creates another focusable control, which increases keyboard effort and cognitive load.
- Set meaningful `minValue`, `maxValue`, and `step` values. The scale should match the precision users actually need.
- Use markers only when there are few enough steps to scan. Tiny steps across a large range can create an excessive number of DOM elements.
- Use `formatOptions` for currency, percentages, measurements, and other locale-sensitive units so values display and announce their meaning.
- Use `description` for persistent guidance and `isRequired` when a value is required.
- Use `isDisabled` when the value should remain visible but unavailable for interaction.
- Use `onChange` for lightweight immediate feedback and `onChangeEnd` for expensive requests, filtering, or calculations.
- Use a text-entry control when exact numeric input is essential. A track is best for exploring or adjusting values within known bounds.

## Props [#props]

### RangeField [#rangefield]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### A thumb is missing a label or form value [#a-thumb-is-missing-a-label-or-form-value]

Check the same index in `thumbLabels` and `thumbNames`. Each array entry renders a thumb, and its accessible label and form name are read from the corresponding positions. A form name does not replace an accessible label.

### TypeScript reports the wrong callback value type [#typescript-reports-the-wrong-callback-value-type]

Keep the controlled or default value and callback signatures consistent. When inference is unavailable, provide the generic explicitly: `<RangeField<number>>` for a scalar or `<RangeField<number[]>>` for an array.

```tsx
const [targets, setTargets] = useState<number[]>([20, 80]);

<RangeField<number[]>
  label="Target range"
  value={targets}
  onChange={setTargets}
  thumbLabels={['Minimum target', 'Maximum target']}
/>;
```

### The controlled thumbs do not move [#the-controlled-thumbs-do-not-move]

The `value` prop is the source of truth. Update the scalar or array in `onChange` without changing its intended shape. For arrays, return a new array so application state observes the update.

### Values snap unexpectedly [#values-snap-unexpectedly]

Verify that `step` represents the intended interval from `minValue`. Every thumb snaps to valid positions on the same configured scale.

### The final marker is missing [#the-final-marker-is-missing]

Markers begin at `minValue` and appear at complete step positions. `maxValue` receives a marker only when the range is evenly divisible by `step`.

### Markers are crowded or rendering is slow [#markers-are-crowded-or-rendering-is-slow]

Increase `step` or omit `markers`. Large ranges with small steps can produce many decorative elements even when users cannot distinguish them visually.

### The value or endpoint labels are blank [#the-value-or-endpoint-labels-are-blank]

Enable automatic current-value output with `valueLabel={true}` or provide custom content. `minLabel` and `maxLabel` display only explicitly supplied content; neither defaults to a numeric bound or receives `formatOptions`.

### Negative values do not behave as expected [#negative-values-do-not-behave-as-expected]

Negative values are supported. Set a negative `minValue` and ensure every scalar or array value remains within the configured bounds.

### The range configuration is invalid [#the-range-configuration-is-invalid]

Provide finite bounds where `minValue` is less than `maxValue`, a finite `step` greater than zero, and finite values inside the configured range.


# Responsive

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- Components adapt to the space they are given with intrinsic CSS and container queries.
- Page layout stays in your CSS, with your own media queries and breakpoints.
- Component sizes can follow `--antares-size`, so your CSS can change them at any breakpoint.
- Responsive styles are plain CSS, so server rendering needs no viewport guess.

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Customization [#customization]

Antares publishes no viewport breakpoints. Components don't change by viewport width, except overlays
such as Modal and Drawer, which document their own thresholds. Choose the breakpoints your layout needs,
and write them in your own media or container queries.

The examples include their CSS in `<style>` blocks so the complete code is visible. Applications can
place those rules in their own stylesheets. Layout props such as `columns` and `gap` write inline styles,
which beat stylesheet rules. When your CSS changes a property across a query, set it in CSS for every
width and leave the prop unset.

A container can't take its width from its content, so give it one from its parent, as the container
example does with the `flex` basis of its sidebar and main area. Otherwise it collapses in flex rows and
other shrink-to-fit layouts. Portaled content is outside the container, so it needs a container in its
own DOM ancestry.

In media queries, `rem` uses the browser's initial font size.

### Responsive size [#responsive-size-1]

Component props, including `size`, take a single value. For a size that changes with the layout, leave
`size` unset and set `--antares-size` in your CSS. TextLockup reads it for its text parts, so you can set
the variable on the lockup itself or an ancestor. The responsive size example sets it on a parent. The
nearest value wins, and an explicit `size` beats it. Without the variable, components follow the
surrounding `SizeProvider`. Browsers without container style queries ignore the variable.

These components follow `--antares-size`:

| Component    | Values     | Notes                               |
| ------------ | ---------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `TextLockup` | `xs`-`2xl` | A `Tag` eyebrow keeps its own size. |

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

Preserve reading order, keyboard focus, and entered values as layouts change: reflow one DOM tree with
CSS instead of rendering different trees. Validate layouts with long text, RTL, narrow widths, text
enlargement, and browser zoom. Resizing the viewport alone does not test every effect of zoom. Use
pointer and hover media features to detect input capabilities, not widths.

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

# Select

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- **Composable interior**: Compose `Label`, a `Button slot="trigger"`, `SelectOptions`, and optional `Text` / `FieldError`. Nothing is added for you, and what you write keeps the order you wrote it in
- **Trigger and options**: An empty `Button slot="trigger"` renders the selected value and a chevron from the field. `SelectOptions` is the list in the popover the Select opens: it takes `ListBox` props (including `items` with a render function for a dynamic collection) plus `popoverProps` for the overlay. Write `Popover`, `Content`, and `ListBox` yourself to replace the whole overlay
- **Composed in another field**: Use `variant="control"` to sit inside another field's `Group`, as a country-code select beside a phone `Input`
- **Single or multiple selection**: Set `selectionMode="multiple"` to allow multiple values
- **Controlled or uncontrolled**: Use `value` and `onChange` for controlled state, or `defaultValue` for uncontrolled
- **Validation states**: Use `isInvalid` with a `FieldError` and `isDisabled` for validation and disabled state
- **Sizes**: The field is a `SizeProvider`. `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) sets the label, trigger, and options, which open at the same size even though they render in a portal. Without it, the Select follows the surrounding scope
- **Form integration**: Set `name` and the value submits as part of a native `<form>` (multiple values submit as repeated entries)
- **React Aria integration**: Built on React Aria Select for accessibility, keyboard navigation, and typeahead

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

```tsx
  <Label />
  <Button slot="trigger" />
  <Text slot="description" />
  <SelectOptions>
    <SelectItem />
  </SelectOptions>
  <FieldError />
</Select>
```

# SizeProvider

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- `sm`, `md`, or `lg` for the adopted components inside (listed below): their text, controls, and
  default spacing.
- The nearest scope wins, and nested scopes replace the size rather than compounding it.
- A component's own `size` prop wins for that component only.
- Overlays opened inside, such as Modal and Select options, open at the scope's size even though
  they render in a portal.
- Renders no element, so it never affects layout. Only Antares components follow it; plain HTML
  keeps its own typography, so put copy in `Text`.
- Without any scope, components use `md`.
- Adopted so far by Text, Detail, Heading, Label, Button, LinkButton, TextField, NumberField, Select,
  DatePicker, DateRangePicker, Calendar, TextLockup, Modal, Drawer, Popover, and Tooltip. Other
  components keep their own size. Layout spacing props keep their meaning: `gap="md"` is the layout
  `md` gap in any scope.

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Props [#props]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />


# Skeleton

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- Height presets from `xs` to `2xl`
- Aspect ratios for images and other media
- Custom width and height for non-standard shapes
- `default`, `full`, and `none` rounding
- A subtle shimmer that reverses in right-to-left locales and stops when reduced motion is preferred
- Composable into text blocks, avatars, cards, and other loading patterns

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

- Every Skeleton is hidden from assistive technology, so a page with many placeholders stays quiet.
- Mark the region the Skeletons fill with `role="status"`, `aria-busy="true"`, and an `aria-label` that describes what is loading.
- Set `aria-busy` to `false`, or remove it, once the real content replaces the Skeletons.
- The shimmer stops when the user prefers reduced motion, and the shape gets an outline in forced colors mode.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Approximate the final layout; a skeleton doesn't need to be pixel-perfect.
- Use size presets for text and basic controls, and `aspectRatio` for images and media.
- Vary the widths of text bars so a paragraph reads like real sentences.
- Match `width` to `size` for squares, and add `full` rounding for circles.

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

- If the shimmer doesn't reverse in a right-to-left app, set `dir="rtl"` on `<html>` or a parent element. Skeleton follows the `dir` attribute, and a locale set only through `I18nProvider` doesn't change it.

## Props [#props]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />


# Structure primitives

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

**Shared structural containers.** These generic, layout-only components are the building blocks for composing a component's interior (a `Modal`, a card, a panel). They are semantic containers built on `Flex`, so they accept the same layout props (`direction`, `gap`, `alignItems`, `justifyContent`, `padding`, ...).

- **`Content`** — the primary body region (a `<section>`, a column that grows to fill).
- **`Header`** — the top region: title area and optional trailing close (a `<header>` row that spaces its contents apart).
- **`Footer`** — the bottom region: secondary content and/or actions (a `<footer>` row that spaces its contents apart).
- **`ButtonGroup`** - a cluster of related actions (a wrapping row with `role="group"`). Overlay parents like `Modal` adopt it with end alignment and padding.
- **`Group`** — semantic grouping container for field item controls. A parent field injects the box chrome.
- **`CornerActions`** - an always-visible structural row for actions placed at a surface corner.

## Hybrid styling [#hybrid-styling]

Each container works in two modes:

- **Standalone** - with no parent context it renders with its own structural defaults and looks the same everywhere.
- **Adopted** - inside a parent that provides its context (e.g. `Modal`), it picks up that parent's styling and spacing automatically. Consumer props still win over the adopted defaults.

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Props [#props]

### Content [#content]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.ContentProps} />

### Header [#header]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.HeaderProps} />

### Footer [#footer]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.FooterProps} />

### ButtonGroup [#buttongroup]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.ButtonGroupProps} />

### Group [#group-1]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.GroupProps} />

### CornerActions [#corneractions]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.CornerActionsProps} />


# Switch

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- Renders a horizontal toggle with a sliding thumb inside a pill-shaped track
- Communicates state to assistive technologies via the WAI-ARIA `switch` role
- Toggles on click or tap anywhere in the control — track, thumb, or label
- Toggles with the `Space` key when focused
- Optional label, positioned at the `start` or `end` of the track, or omitted entirely
- Two sizes: `md` (default) and `sm`
- Supports controlled (`isSelected` + `onChange`) and uncontrolled (`defaultSelected`) usage
- Takes effect immediately — no form submission required

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Customization [#customization]

### Data Attributes [#data-attributes]

The interactive switch control exposes data attributes for styling different states:

`data-selected`, `data-hovered`, `data-pressed`, `data-focused`, `data-focus-visible`, `data-disabled`, `data-readonly`, `data-invalid`, `data-required`, `data-size`

```css
.my-switch [data-focus-visible] {
  outline: 2px solid Highlight;
}

.my-switch [data-disabled] {
  opacity: 0.4;
  cursor: not-allowed;
}
```

### Design Tokens [#design-tokens]

The track and thumb read from Antares curated tokens, falling back to legacy `--ux-*` custom properties:

| Element | Token | Legacy fallback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Track (off) | — | `--ux-1m9ys0v` |
| Track (on) | `--color-input-background-selected` | `--ux-sywk25` |
| Thumb | `--color-input-background-default` | `--ux-1nu8itt` |
| Thumb inset | — | `--ux-1sbfig8` |
| Label | `--color-input-text-default` | `--ux-1glcx6s` |
| Focus ring radius | — | `--ux-zvaw3s` |

### Component Customization [#component-customization]

Pass a `className` or `style` to customize the field container. Target the interactive descendant's data attributes for state-based styling:

```jsx
<Switch className="custom-switch">Wi-Fi</Switch>
```

Use the interactive root data attributes for state-based customization. The track and thumb are internal implementation details and do not expose class-name hooks.

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

- Renders with the WAI-ARIA `switch` role via the native `<input type="checkbox" role="switch">`
- `Space` toggles the switch when it has focus
- Displays a visible focus ring (`outline: 2px solid Highlight`) for keyboard focus
- Disabled switches render at `40%` opacity and are excluded from tab order
- When `children` is omitted, provide `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` so the switch has an accessible name

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

### When to Use Switch [#when-to-use-switch]

- ✅ For settings that take effect immediately, without a form submission
- ✅ For binary on/off preferences (e.g. Wi-Fi, notifications, dark mode)
- ❌ For selections that require a "Save" or "Submit" action (use `Checkbox` instead)
- ❌ For choosing one of several mutually exclusive options (use `Radio` or `SegmentedController` instead)

### Labeling [#labeling]

- Prefer a visible label that names the setting being toggled (e.g. "Wi-Fi", not "On/Off")
- If the label is omitted, always provide `aria-label`
- Keep labels short and describe the setting, not its current state

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### Controlled State Not Updating [#controlled-state-not-updating]

```jsx
// ❌ Wrong: isSelected without onChange leaves the switch stuck
<Switch isSelected={isOn}>Wi-Fi</Switch>

// ✅ Controlled mode
<Switch isSelected={isOn} onChange={setIsOn}>Wi-Fi</Switch>

// ✅ Uncontrolled mode
<Switch defaultSelected>Wi-Fi</Switch>
```

### Missing Accessible Name [#missing-accessible-name]

```jsx
// ❌ No children and no aria-label — screen readers announce nothing useful
<Switch />

// ✅ Provide a label
<Switch>Wi-Fi</Switch>

// ✅ Or an aria-label when the label is visual-only elsewhere
<Switch aria-label="Wi-Fi" />
```

## Props [#props]

### Switch [#switch]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />


# Tabs

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- Accessible Tabs semantics powered by React Aria Components.
- Underline and Manilla visual treatments.
- Controlled and uncontrolled selection.
- Automatic horizontal overflow controls that move one tab at a time.
- Localized labels for the automatic overflow controls.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

Tabs require an accessible label on `TabList`. Use the keyboard to move between tabs with the arrow keys. Disabled tabs are skipped. Use `keyboardActivation="manual"` when focus should move independently of selection.

`overflowLabels` is optional and defaults to "Previous tabs" and "Next tabs". Provide localized labels when needed; they should describe the logical direction rather than physical directions like "left" or "right", as the component automatically handles RTL layouts.

`TabList` must be rendered inside `Tabs` and must provide `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. Give each `Tab` and its corresponding `TabPanel` the same `id`; React Aria uses that key to build their accessible relationship.

## Customization [#customization]

The component exposes state through data attributes:

- `Tabs`: `data-design="underline"` or `data-design="manilla"`.
- `Tab`: `data-selected`, `data-hovered`, `data-pressed`, `data-focus-visible`, and `data-disabled`.
- `TabPanel`: `data-inert` when a force-mounted inactive panel is not interactive.

Use these attributes to extend styling without replacing the accessibility behavior supplied by React Aria Components. You can also use render props in `className` to style based on state (e.g., `className={({ isSelected }) => isSelected ? 'active' : ''}`).

Use `TabList`'s `containerProps` to customize the outer tab list shell, such as increasing its width.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Use Tabs for peer panels on the same page and URL.
- Keep the number of tabs small enough for users to understand the available sections.
- Do not use Tabs for primary application navigation or route changes.
- Do not render a standalone `Tab`; compose it inside `Tabs` and `TabList`.

## Props [#props]

```tsx
<Tabs>
  <TabList>
    <Tab />
  </TabList>
  <TabPanels>
    <TabPanel />
  </TabPanels>
</Tabs>
```

### Tabs [#tabs]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />

### TabList [#tablist]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.TabListProps} />

### Tab [#tab]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.TabProps} />

### TabPanels [#tabpanels]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.TabPanelsProps} />

### TabPanel [#tabpanel]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.TabPanelProps} />


# Tag

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Screen readers [#screen-readers]

Tags are `<span>` elements with no special ARIA role. Screen readers announce the tag's text as part of normal page content — no extra markup is needed.

### Decorative icons [#decorative-icons]

Icons passed as children must include `aria-hidden="true"` so they are skipped by screen readers. The text label is the sole carrier of meaning.

```tsx
<Tag emphasis="critical">
  <Icon icon="alert" aria-hidden="true" />
  Expired
</Tag>
```

### Indicator dot [#indicator-dot]

The colored dot is decorative and invisible to screen readers. The text label must convey the status on its own — never rely on the dot alone to communicate meaning.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Use the indicator style in dense layouts like tables and dashboards. Use the filled style when the tag is a prominent, standalone element on a card or hero section.
- Default to the small size in compact layouts like tables and lists. Use medium or large only when the tag needs to stand out as a primary piece of information.
- Use the inline design only within running prose. In grouped or standalone contexts, the filled style provides better visual separation.
- Do not stack multiple tags of different emphasis on the same item. Choose the most important one — too many competing labels lose their meaning.

## When to Use [#when-to-use]

- Showing the status of an item on a card, table row, or list entry (e.g. "Active", "Expired", "Pending")
- Categorizing or grouping content so users can scan and filter quickly (e.g. "New", "Sale", "Beta")
- Surfacing metadata about an item (e.g. "Pro", "Free trial", "Internal")
- Communicating priority or category in project management and collaboration tools (e.g. "High priority", "In review")

## When Not to Use [#when-not-to-use]

- If users need to click or dismiss it — use a **Button** instead.
- If the label is part of a sentence with no visual distinction — just use text.

## Props [#props]

### Tag [#tag]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />

# TextField

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- **Composable interior**: Compose `Label`, `Input` or `TextArea`, `Text slot="description"`, and `FieldError`. Omitting `Group` leaves the control as a direct field child with box chrome. Use an explicit `Group` for controls or adornments
- **Adornments**: Fixed text or icons before or after the input (e.g. `$`, `.00`, `px`) are composed inside `Group`, positioned by source order
- **Controls**: A `Button slot="control"` beside the input is an interactive affix; it picks up field chrome from context
- **Controlled or uncontrolled**: Use `value` and `onChange` for controlled state, or `defaultValue` for uncontrolled
- **Multiline**: Compose a `TextArea` instead of an `Input` for multiline entry
- **Validation states**: Use `isInvalid` with a `FieldError` and `isDisabled` for validation and disabled state
- **Sizes**: The field is a `SizeProvider`. `size` (`sm`, `md`, `lg`) sets its label, input, description, error, and composed controls; without it, the field follows the surrounding scope. An explicit `size` on a part still wins for that part

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Blocks [#blocks]

<BlockLink id="sign-in-form" />

## Props [#props]

```tsx
<TextField>
  <Label />
  <Input />
  {/* or <TextArea /> */}
  {/* or <Group><Input /></Group> for adornments or a control */}
  <Text slot="description" />
  <FieldError />
</TextField>
```

### TextField [#textfield]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />


# TextLockup

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Features [#features]

- Six coordinated sizes, from a `2xl` page title down to `xs`
- An eyebrow that takes plain text or a `Tag`, sized to match the lockup
- Slotted parts, so nested components keep their own type
- Any heading level, chosen independently of the visual size
- Start or center alignment
- A legible line-length clamp, on by default

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Customization [#customization]

`TextLockup` positions and type-sets its parts; you supply them. That means anything else can
sit alongside them — a call to action, a second paragraph, an image — without the component
growing a prop for it.

- **Every part names its role with a slot**: `eyebrow`, `title`, `body`. Unslotted text follows
  the lockup's tier too: a bare `Heading` takes the title tier and a bare `Text` the body tier.
- **The eyebrow is `slot="eyebrow"`**, on either a `Text` or a `Tag`. The two forms swap
  freely, and a `Tag` is sized to pair with the lockup.
- **The title is `<Heading slot="title">`.** Pick the level from the document outline, not the
  visual size: `size` handles the visuals, so `level={1}` in an `xs` lockup is perfectly valid.
- **The body is `<Text slot="body">`**, once or as many times as the copy needs.
- **An explicit prop on a child always wins** over what the lockup supplies. Pass
  `<Tag slot="eyebrow" size="sm">` to break the pairing, for instance.
- **Controls keep the scale size.** A `Button` inside a lockup follows the surrounding
  `SizeProvider` or its own `size` prop, never the lockup's tier.
- **`size` is the tier.** The eyebrow reads it on the `detail` ramp, the title on `heading`, and
  the body on `body`, so there is no table to memorize. Without `size`, the lockup follows the
  surrounding size scope. A tier is the same at every container width.
- Pass `className` to extend the styles, or select on `[data-align]`.

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

- The title carries the heading semantics. Choose `level` so the page outline stays correct
  rather than to achieve a size.
- Slots resolve against the lockup, so `slot="title"` names the lockup's title, not an outer
  container's. Inside a
  `Modal`, `Drawer` or `Popover`, give the dialog its own `<Heading slot="title">` as a direct
  child for the accessible name, and use the lockup for the body.
- The eyebrow is decorative in most designs. If it carries meaning, make sure the title still
  reads sensibly on its own, since screen reader users often navigate by heading.

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Use one `2xl` lockup per page at most — it is the page title.
- Keep `legibleLines` on for running prose. Turn it off only when the lockup already sits in a
  narrow column, where the clamp does nothing but complicate the layout.
- Prefer a `Tag` eyebrow for status or category, and plain text for a kicker or section label.
- Reach for `MetricsLockup` instead when the emphasis is a single number rather than prose.

## Props [#props]

Place the title directly inside `TextLockup` when there are no corner actions. The eyebrow can
be `Text` or `Tag` and comes before the title.

```tsx
<TextLockup>
  <Tag slot="eyebrow" />
  <Heading slot="title" />
  <Text slot="body" />
  {/* ... */}
</TextLockup>
```

Wrap the title in `Header` when using `CornerActions`.

```tsx
<TextLockup>
  <Tag slot="eyebrow" />
  <Header>
    <CornerActions />
    <Heading slot="title" />
  </Header>
  <Text slot="body" />
  {/* ... */}
</TextLockup>
```

### TextLockup [#textlockup]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />


# Text

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

`Text` is body copy and `Detail` is supporting copy: captions, metadata, and hints.

## Features [#features]

- `Text` applies the body role and `Detail` the detail role, each at the tier of the nearest
  `SizeProvider`, or `md` outside any scope.
- Inside a component's named part, such as a field description or a lockup body, the part sets the
  treatment. Inside a control, the label keeps the control's type, so
  `<Button><Text>Save</Text></Button>` looks exactly like `<Button>Save</Button>`.
- `size` picks a step on the component's own ramp (`xs` to `2xl`) and changes only the font size.
- `emphasis` picks a feedback color and changes only the color.
- For semantic emphasis, render `as="strong"` or `as="em"`.

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Props [#props]

### Text [#text]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />

### Detail [#detail-1]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.DetailProps} />


# ToggleButton

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Customization [#customization]

### Data Attributes [#data-attributes]

Components automatically add data attributes for styling different states:

**ToggleButtonGroup Container:** `data-size`

**ToggleButton Item:** `data-selected`, `data-hovered`, `data-pressed`, `data-focus-visible`, `data-disabled`

```css
.my-toggle-group [data-selected] {
  background-color: #09757a;
  color: #fff;
}

.my-toggle-group [data-focus-visible] {
  outline: 2px solid #1976d2;
  outline-offset: 2px;
}

.my-toggle-group [data-disabled] {
  opacity: 0.4;
  cursor: not-allowed;
}
```

### Component Customization [#component-customization]

Individual components can be styled by passing `className` props:

```jsx
<ToggleButtonGroup aria-label="View" className="custom-toggle-group">
  <ToggleButton id="list" className="custom-item">List</ToggleButton>
  <ToggleButton id="grid" className="custom-item">Grid</ToggleButton>
</ToggleButtonGroup>
```

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard Navigation [#keyboard-navigation]

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| **Tab** | Moves focus to/from the button group (single tab stop) |
| **Arrow Left / Right** | Move focus between items (RAC automatically reverses in RTL) |
| **Space / Enter** | Toggle the focused item |
| **Home** | Move focus to the first item |
| **End** | Move focus to the last item |

### ARIA Support [#aria-support]

- `selectionMode="single"` → `role="radiogroup"` on container, `role="radio"` + `aria-checked` per item
- `selectionMode="multiple"` → `role="toolbar"` on container, `role="button"` + `aria-pressed` per item
- `aria-label` (or `aria-labelledby`) is required on the group container
- Icon-only items require `aria-label` on each `ToggleButton`

## Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

### Selection Not Updating [#selection-not-updating]

```jsx
// ❌ Wrong: Using both selectedKeys and defaultSelectedKeys
<ToggleButtonGroup selectedKeys={keys} defaultSelectedKeys={['day']}>
  <ToggleButton id="day">Day</ToggleButton>
</ToggleButtonGroup>

// ✅ Controlled mode
<ToggleButtonGroup selectedKeys={keys} onSelectionChange={setKeys}>
  <ToggleButton id="day">Day</ToggleButton>
</ToggleButtonGroup>

// ✅ Uncontrolled mode
<ToggleButtonGroup defaultSelectedKeys={['day']}>
  <ToggleButton id="day">Day</ToggleButton>
</ToggleButtonGroup>
```

### Styling Overrides Not Applying [#styling-overrides-not-applying]

```css
/* ❌ May not have enough specificity */
.my-custom-item {
  background-color: red;
}

/* ✅ Use data attributes with className for higher specificity */
.my-toggle-group [data-selected] {
  background-color: red;
}
```

### Keyboard Navigation Not Working [#keyboard-navigation-not-working]

```css
/* ❌ Don't remove focus outlines without replacement */
[data-focus-visible] {
  outline: none;
}

/* ✅ Provide visible focus indicator */
.my-toggle-group [data-focus-visible] {
  outline: 2px solid #1976d2;
  outline-offset: 2px;
}
```

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

### When to Use [#when-to-use]

- ✅ For grouped contextual actions — two or more closely related actions that belong together (e.g. Bold / Italic / Underline, Align Left / Center / Right)
- ✅ For compact action grouping — related actions in space-constrained layouts (e.g. Undo / Redo, Zoom In / Out / Reset)
- ✅ For multi-select scenarios — when users need to select multiple options simultaneously
- ❌ For unrelated actions that perform disconnected tasks without shared context
- ❌ For more than 5 choices — cognitive overload; consider a **Select** instead
- ❌ When actions require strong visual distinction (e.g. Save vs. Delete)
- ❌ When selecting an option leads to a different page or workflow — use navigation instead
- ❌ For mutually exclusive content views (e.g. Monthly / Yearly) — use **SegmentedController** instead

### Keep Variants Consistent [#keep-variants-consistent]

Avoid mixing different content types (text-only, icon-only, icon+text) within the same group. Mixing styles creates visual noise and makes the set feel fragmented rather than unified.

### Balance Label Lengths [#balance-label-lengths]

Keep button labels of similar length. Large differences in text length cause irregular button widths and make the group appear uneven. Prefer short, concise wording.

### Alignment [#alignment]

Align the group to reflect its relationship to surrounding content:

- **Left** — when the group controls content directly below or within the same column (dashboards, tables).
- **Center** — when the group acts as a prominent toggle affecting an entire section or page.
- **Right** — when the group represents utility or contextual controls (e.g. grid/list view toggle).

### Label Guidelines [#label-guidelines]

- Use **title case**: capitalize the first letter of each word, except short prepositions.
- Keep labels to one or two words. Omit articles (a, an, the) and filler words.
- Prefer action-focused or descriptive language that communicates the option instantly.

### Icon-Only Items [#icon-only-items]

Use icon-only items only when the icon's meaning is universally recognized. Always provide an `aria-label` on each icon-only `ToggleButton`:

```tsx
<ToggleButton id="list" aria-label="List view">
  <Icon icon="bulleted-list" />
</ToggleButton>
```

## Props [#props]

```tsx
<ToggleButtonGroup>
  <ToggleButton />
  {/* ... */}
</ToggleButtonGroup>
```

### ToggleButtonGroup [#togglebuttongroup]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.Props} />

### ToggleButton [#togglebutton]

<ArgTypes of={Stories.ToggleButtonProps} />


# Tooltip

<Meta of={Stories} name="Overview" />

Tooltips appear after a short delay when hovering, and immediately when the element receives focus.
Once a tooltip has been shown, subsequent tooltips appear without delay.

`TooltipTrigger` wraps a focusable element and a `<Tooltip>`, handling hover/focus state and positioning automatically.

## Features [#features]

- `overlay` elevation panel positioned relative to its trigger, with an optional arrow
- Flips and shifts to stay in the viewport
- Configurable open and close delays

## Installation [#installation]

```bash
npm install --save @godaddy/antares
```

## Examples [#examples]

<Examples of={Stories.Examples} />

## Customization [#customization]

`className` and `style` apply to the tooltip panel.

## Accessibility [#accessibility]

### Keyboard [#keyboard]

| Key      | Action                                                     |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Tab`    | Moves focus to the focusable element and shows the tooltip |
| `Escape` | Closes the tooltip                                         |

### ARIA [#aria]

- The tooltip uses `role="tooltip"` and is associated with its focusable element via `aria-describedby`

## Best Practices [#best-practices]

- Keep tooltip content short and informative.
- Tooltips are not shown on touch screen interactions. Ensure your UI is usable without tooltips.
- Do not place interactive content inside tooltips. Use a `Popover` instead.

## Props [#props]

```tsx
<TooltipTrigger>
  <Button />
  <Tooltip placement="bottom" />
</TooltipTrigger>
```

# Build product experiences with Antares.

<Meta title="Blocks" id="blocks" />

## Install a block [#install-a-block]

From the root of your application, run the command copied by the block's Install button:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add godaddy/antares/blocks/sign-in-form
```
